documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) supports the development of novel halal foods, including plant-based and cultivated alternatives, offering environmentally sustainable and cost-effective solutions to global food security challenges. While facilitating innovation and strengthening consumer trust, these advancements also raise significant ethical, regulatory, and religious concerns in Muslim contexts where compliance with Sharīʿah principles is essential. This study aims to examine how AI-enabled food innovations can align with Sharīʿah requirements while safeguarding halal integrity and consumer confidence. Employing a conceptual review methodology, the paper synthesizes Qur’anic and ḥadīth-based principles with contemporary scholarly literature and regulatory frameworks on AI integration, halal certification, and novel food governance. The study addresses a critical research gap concerning the absence of comprehensive Sharīʿah-based guidelines and harmonised regulatory standards for AI-driven novel foods, particularly in relation to certification, traceability, and consumer assurance. The analysis yields three key findings: (1) AI technologies enhance halal assurance systems through improved traceability, transparency, and risk management; (2) AI-enabled novel foods may be considered permissible under the concept of bidʿah ḥasanah (beneficial innovation) when their ingredients and production processes comply with established Sharīʿah principles; and (3) inadequate regulatory oversight and the lack of standardised certification frameworks pose risks to halal integrity and may erode consumer trust. The study concludes that responsible integration of AI in novel food innovation requires coupling technological advancement with robust Islamic ethical governance and recommends the development of harmonised standards through collaboration among halal authorities, policymakers, and industry stakeholders.

Abstract Surgical artificial intelligence (AI) is typically validated on one patient population and then deployed unchanged into another, without surgeon input into its design. AI in orthopaedics should be built with surgeons, not simply for them: Surgeons should hold shared authority over the clinical question, data curation, validation, implementation, monitoring and retirement of any tool they use. Specialty‐tuned models outperform general‐purpose systems on some tasks, but the margin is modest and likely to narrow as generalist models improve. The more durable distinction is who controls the update loop—who can retrain a model on local outcomes, audit its failures and withdraw it when it drifts. Trial evidence shows that a clinician kept in that loop by design, not as an afterthought, outperforms working alone. What determines whether orthopaedic AI fulfils its promise is not model architecture, but who stays accountable to the surgeon at the bedside when the model needs to change.

documents.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is embedded in every financial transaction and interaction through robo-advising, auto- Recommendations, portfolios tracking, digital financial assistants, and financial information processing tools. This paper considers the relevance of AI to young investors of the Kalyan Region. Using relevant published evidence from SEBI, NSE, AMFI and RBI, along with peer-reviewed research and analysis, this paper applies descriptive, comparative and trend-oriented analysis to examine the use and impact of AI in personal finance management. Evidence shows an ageing-down of India's investor base, with young people constituting an increasing proportion of the registered individual investors. The study finds that AI can reduce information and access barriers and enable personalisation, monitoring, and analysis. However, the benefits are limited by financial literacy, trust, perceived risk, transparency and ability to question AI outputs.

Abstract The chemical industry is essential for modern society, but conventional chemical processes may require substantial quantities of energy, solvents and raw materials and can generate undesirable waste and emissions. Sustainable chemistry seeks to address these concerns by designing chemical products and processes that use resources more efficiently and reduce environmental and health risks. In parallel, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for analysing complex chemical information, predicting molecular and material properties, optimizing reactions and supporting scientific decision-making. The integration of AI with sustainable chemistry creates an opportunity to accelerate the development of safer, cleaner and more resource-efficient chemical technologies. This review examines the emerging role of AI in sustainable chemistry, with particular emphasis on machine learning, predictive modelling, reaction optimization, catalyst discovery, solvent selection, sustainable materials, carbon management, green hydrogen, waste valorization and analytical chemistry. The potential of AI to support the principles of green chemistry and life-cycle-based decision-making is also discussed. Recent studies indicate that AI can reduce experimental effort and improve the efficiency of chemical discovery and process development, although limitations related to data quality, interpretability, validation, computational requirements and industrial scale-up remain significant. The review further considers the relevance of AI-enabled sustainable chemistry to India's long-term development objectives under Viksit Bharat @2047. A future-oriented framework for responsible AI-driven chemistry is proposed, emphasizing scientific validation, environmental assessment, interdisciplinary collaboration and indigenous innovation.

Artificial intelligence plays a crucial role today by assisting providers in patient care and supporting them in various intelligent healthcare systems. The technique shifts from computational knowledge to machine learning, which can assess complex medical data. AI is ubiquitous in Healthcare, which can be used in treatment, diagnosis, patient risk identification, and predicting the outcome of clinical scenarios. An overview of different intelligent techniques presented in this article is discussed with the receiver of clinical application, and future challenges of the current scenario of AI in Healthcare. Articles and internet searches were carried out using the keywords Artificial Intelligence and computational Healthcare. Further references were obtained from Data available on Google Scholar, PubMed, medical databases, and cross-referencing from key articles based on it. The results are also assessed using a variety of quality standards, including prediction accuracy and rate, based on the examination of several papers on disease diagnosis.

documents.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping analytical chemistry by changing how instrumental measurements are processed, interpreted, optimized, and translated into chemical decisions. Modern analytical platforms generate high-dimensional spectra, chromatograms, mass spectra, images, and sensor signals in volumes that can exceed the practical capacity of conventional univariate or manually supervised workflows. This integrative review examines AI-driven advances across spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), chemical sensors, imaging, and analytical method development. The review adopts a structured narrative design using purposive sampling of peer-reviewed reviews, primary methodological literature, and regulatory guidance identified through targeted searches of major biomedical and chemistry literature sources and official regulatory repositories. Evidence was thematically coded into four domains: data enhancement, predictive modelling, analytical-method optimization, and decision support. The synthesis indicates that machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), chemometrics, quantitative structure–retention relationships (QSRR), and hybrid mechanistic–data-driven approaches can improve pattern recognition, spectral deconvolution, analyte identification, retention prediction, calibration, anomaly detection, and experimental optimization when adequate and representative data are available. However, AI does not automatically create a valid analytical method: model leakage, biased sampling, poor external validation, instrument drift, explainability limitations, and weak uncertainty characterization can undermine apparent performance. Current regulatory thinking increasingly emphasizes risk-based credibility and conventional analytical validation principles. Future analytical laboratories are therefore likely to combine AI with robust metrology, automated experimentation, digital twins, explainable AI, multimodal data fusion, and continuous lifecycle validation. The central conclusion is that the strongest pathway is not replacement of analytical chemistry by AI, but integration of chemical knowledge, measurement science, and trustworthy computation.

The increasing use of artificial intelligence in audit practice has begun to reshape how audit tasks are performed, yet evidence on its implications for auditor performance remains limited, particularly in developing economies. This study investigates the relationship between artificial intelligence-driven audit technology and auditor performance in listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. Drawing on Task-Technology Fit Theory, AI-driven audit technology is examined through three functional dimensions, namely AI-based audit analytics, machine learning-enabled fraud detection systems, and robotic process automation in audit tasks, while auditor experience is incorporated as a control variable. The study employs a quantitative cross-sectional survey approach using data obtained from 410 audit professionals. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling with SmartPLS 4, following a two-stage procedure involving measurement and structural model assessment. The findings show that AI-based audit analytics, machine learning-enabled fraud detection systems, and robotic process automation each have a positive and statistically significant relationship with auditor performance. Auditor experience also demonstrates a significant positive influence, indicating that professional expertise complements, rather than replaces, the use of advanced audit technologies. Overall, the results provide empirical evidence that the effective alignment of technological capabilities with audit task requirements enhances auditor performance within the banking sector. The study contributes to auditing literature by offering evidence on the performance effects of disaggregated AI-driven audit technologies in a developing economy and highlights the practical importance of investing in both advanced audit tools and continuous professional development.

Background: Automated facial analysis has the potential to standardize orthodontic assessment by minimizing human error and variability. Prior work (Rousseau et al., 2022) compared AI-based and manual methods using only four landmarks and three ratios, leaving broader anthropometric evaluation unexplored.Objective: To validate an automated workflow that extracts sixteen facial landmarks, computes twenty-two anthropometric ratios and three vertical proportions from 2D clinical photographs, and to compare its reliability against manual measurements.Materials and Methods: One hundred patients (15–25 years) without craniofacial anomalies were enrolled. Two operators placed sixteen landmarks and computed all ratios and proportions twice to assess intra- and inter-rater reliability. The AI pipeline used a custom Python script integrating Mediapipe’s facial-landmark model. Reliability was quantified by intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs), and agreement between manual and AI measurements was examined via Bland–Altman analysis.Results: Manual intrarater ICCs exceeded 0.90 for 18 of 22 ratios and all vertical proportions, indicating excellent repeatability. Interrater ICCs were > 0.90 for seven ratios, 0.75–0.90 for ten, 0.50–0.75 for four, and < 0.50 for one; vertical-proportion ICCs ranged from 0.08 to 0.75. The AI workflow produced mean differences under 2 % compared to manual values, with 95 % of differences within Bland–Altman limits, demonstrating minimal systematic bias.Conclusions: The AI-driven method reliably reproduces manual anthropometric measurements across an expanded metric set, reducing operator variability and analysis time. This objective tool shows promise for standardized orthodontic evaluation. Future studies should test larger, multiethnic cohorts, extend to three-dimensional imaging, and assess routine clinical integration.

The rapid advancement of nanomedicine has improved drug delivery; however, conventional nanoparticle development remains limited by trial-and-error optimization, scalability constraints, and environmental concerns. Green nanotechnology offers a sustainable alternative through the use of biodegradable materials, renewable precursors, and environmentally benign synthesis approaches. Among emerging sustainable nanomaterials, green carbon dots have attracted increasing interest because of their biocompatibility, tunable surface chemistry, intrinsic fluorescence, and relatively low toxicity. Nevertheless, precise control of their physicochemical and biological properties remains challenging. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and data-driven modeling, provides opportunities for predictive formulation design, optimization of nanocarrier properties, and reduction of experimental burden. The integration of AI with sustainable nanomedicine therefore offers a promising strategy for developing intelligent drug delivery systems with improved therapeutic precision, targeting, controlled drug release, and bioimaging capabilities. This review critically examines the convergence of AI and sustainable nanomedicine, with particular emphasis on green carbon dots for smart drug delivery. It discusses green synthesis strategies, AI-driven nanocarrier design and optimization, intelligent targeting, controlled drug delivery, bioimaging applications, and translational challenges. Future perspectives concerning scalability, reproducibility, regulatory considerations, and environmentally responsible manufacturing are also addressed, highlighting the potential of AI-enabled green carbon dots as a sustainable platform for next-generation drug delivery.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming accounting practice by displacing traditional data-processing tasks, augmenting auditing functions, and reshaping the professional competency requirements of financial reporting. While these technological developments generate substantial efficiency gains, they simultaneously introduce unprecedented ethical challenges, including algorithmic opacity, accountability diffusion, bias propagation in automated judgment, and the erosion of professional scepticism — that threaten the integrity of financial reporting and the public trust upon which the accounting profession's social licence to operate ultimately depends. This paper develops a rigorous, theoretically grounded analysis of the intersection between artificial intelligence and accounting ethics, drawing on institutional theory, agency theory, virtue ethics, and the stakeholder trust framework to diagnose how AI adoption reconfigures the ethical architecture of financial reporting and to prescribe the governance, professional, and regulatory responses required to safeguard ethical standards and trust in this transformed environment. The paper makes three original contributions: first, it develops a multi-dimensional taxonomy of AI-related ethical risks in accounting, distinguishing technical, professional, and systemic risk categories; second, it proposes the Ethical AI Accounting Governance Framework (EAAGF), an original implementation model that integrates algorithmic governance, professional ethics renewal, regulatory adaptation, and stakeholder assurance mechanisms; and third, it situates these contributions within a comparative empirical analysis of AI adoption experiences across major accounting contexts, integrating evidence from surveys, regulatory reports, and case illustrations. The paper argues that the central challenge is not whether AI will transform accounting — this is already occurring — but whether the profession, regulators, and organisations can collectively construct the ethical governance infrastructure required to ensure that transformation advances rather than undermines the accountability, transparency, and trust that constitute the profession's foundational social purpose.

documents.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) remain a major occupational health concern among office employees, despite growing awareness of workplace ergonomics. Evidence on the relationship between workstation ergonomic risk and musculoskeletal symptoms among university administrative staff remains limited. This study evaluated ergonomic risk using the Rapid Office Strain Assessment (ROSA), determined the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms, and examined their associations with workstation ergonomic risk and work-related factors among administrative staff at a Malaysian public university. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 54 full-time administrative employees selected through simple random sampling. Workstation ergonomic risk was assessed using ROSA, and musculoskeletal symptoms were measured using the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ). Descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, Spearman’s rank correlation, and linear regression analyses were conducted in SPSS version 27, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. The mean ROSA score was 2.93 ± 0.82, with 77.8% of workstations classified as low risk. Despite this, 96.3% of participants reported at least one musculoskeletal symptom, most commonly in the lower back (79.6%), neck (74.1%), and upper back (72.2%). No significant association was found between ROSA scores and MSD symptoms. Multiple regression identified years of employment (β = 0.453, p = 0.024), frequent bending (β = 4.875, p = 0.045), and arm and hand exertion (β =− 3.790, p = 0.028) as independent predictors of total symptom scores. These findings suggest that cumulative occupational exposure and work demands may contribute more substantially to musculoskeletal symptoms than workstation ergonomic risk alone. Comprehensive ergonomic interventions integrating workstation optimisation, work organisation, and ergonomic education are recommended to reduce the MSD burden and improve occupational health among university administrative staff.

Poor performance in fractions remains a major concern in mathematics education because fraction knowledge is fundamental to developing foundational and advanced mathematical skills. This study examined the association between pupils’ poor performance in fractions and the acquisition of mathematical skills in the Sagnarigu Municipality of Ghana. Grounded in constructivist learning theory, the study employed a concurrent mixed-methods cross-sectional design. Quantitative data were collected from 150 basic school mathematics teachers using a structured questionnaire, while qualitative data were obtained through interviews with 10 Basic Education Certificate Examination candidates. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and regression analysis, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Results revealed a statistically significant association between teachers’ perceptions of pupils’ fraction performance and the acquisition of advanced mathematical skills. Cognitive engagement and teacher-related factors were positively associated with mathematical skill acquisition, whereas socioeconomic challenges, environmental constraints, and inadequate instructional practices were associated with poorer mathematics learning outcomes. Qualitative findings revealed pupils’ difficulties in understanding and applying fractions to other mathematical concepts and highlighted the importance of instructional approaches, practice opportunities, learning resources, and learning environments. The study concludes that difficulties with fractions are significantly associated with weaknesses in foundational and advanced mathematical skills, highlighting the need for improved fraction instruction and supportive learning environments. Key words: Advanced-mathematics, common fractions, effects, foundational mathematics, performance.
topics: Cognitive and developmental aspects of mathematical skills

documents.abstract: Objective: to characterize the physical activity profile, frequency, duration, intensity, and modalities — of pilots from the Transport, Patrol, and Reconnaissance Aviations of the Brazilian Air Force (BAF) and to discuss its implications for occupational health, sedentary behavior, and operational human performance. Method: cross-sectional observational epidemiological study, with a quantitative approach, conducted with 483 pilots reporting flight experience in these aviation categories, among the 35 Aviation Groups. Data were collected between May and July 2023 through an electronic questionnaire structured from the conceptual framework of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), with intensity operationalized through self-reported subjective categories; analyses were performed in IBM SPSS Statistics (α = 0.05). The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee (Opinion No. 6,147,313). Results: the sample was predominantly male (97.5%), with a mean age of 30.15 ± 4.87 years, and 29.0% had accumulated more than 1,200 flight hours. A predominantly active but heterogeneous profile was observed: 22.4% did not perform strength training, the highest proportion among BAF specialties — whereas 58.1% trained at least three times per week. In the cardiorespiratory component, 84.7% were practitioners, but the largest share (37.7%) exercised only once or twice a week. Weight training predominated in strengthening (80.8%), with low adherence to core training (2.1%) and Pilates (1.8%). Conclusion: despite the active profile, gaps in regularity and specificity persist which, combined with the sedentary behavior inherent to the mission, indicate the need for differentiated physical preparation programs aimed at preserving health and operational readiness.

Sign language recognition is an important assistive technology for improving communication accessibility for individuals with hearing and speech impairments. While recent deep learning models have achieved impressive recognition accuracy, they often operate as ”black boxes”. This lack of transparency limits their trustworthiness and adoption in real-world assistive technologies. To address this, we introduce an explainability-aligned hybrid framework that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformers for interpretable Indian Sign Language (ISL) recognition. Our architecture pairs an EfficientNet-based convolutional branch, designed to capture fine-grained, local hand features with a Shifted Window Transformer (Swin Transformer) branch that models global contextual relationships. Further, to ensure the model’s decisions make intuitive sense, we introduce a learnable explanation-alignment mechanism. This mechanism uses an explanation-alignment loss and an adaptive gating strategy to enforce spatial consistency between the CNN’s saliency maps and the Transformer’s attention representations. To evaluate the proposed approach, a new Indian Sign Language dataset containing 82,500 images from 33 sign classes was developed and assessed using a subject-independent evaluation protocol. The proposed framework achieved 99.85 ± 0.06 % classification accuracy and 99.99 ± 0.05 % Macro-F1 (macro-averaged F1-score), outperforming standalone Convolutional Neural Network, Transformer, and conventional hybrid architectures. Furthermore, explainability assessments using deletion faithfulness and weakly supervised object localization metrics confirm that our approach generates more reliable, well-focused, and spatially coherent visual explanations. The findings suggest that incorporating explanation alignment into hybrid learning architectures can simultaneously improve recognition accuracy and explanation quality, providing a promising step toward more trustworthy and interpretable Artificial Intelligence systems for sign language recognition.

Background Understanding patients’ experiences is essential for advancing patient-centered care, especially in chronic diseases that require ongoing communication. Qualitative thematic analysis is widely used to explore these experiences; however, the process remains labor-intensive, subjective, and difficult to scale. Objective This study aimed to develop and evaluate Collaborative Theme Identification Agents (CoTI), a multiagent large language model framework designed to support manual thematic analysis by rapidly generating supporting excerpts, initial codes, and themes. Methods CoTI consists of 3 agents: Instructor, Thematizer, and CodebookGenerator. The Instructor refines instruction prompts, the Thematizer extracts supporting excerpts and generates initial codes for each transcript, and the CodebookGenerator groups similar codes across all transcripts into a codebook with themes. We evaluated CoTI primarily using 12 transcripts of patient with heart failure, with a focus on perceptions of medication intensity. CoTI-generated outputs were compared against the reference standard developed by senior investigators. To explore human-AI interaction in thematic analyses, we further implemented CoTI in a user-facing application. Results CoTI generated supporting excerpts, initial codes, and themes that were more similar to those of senior investigators than were the outputs of junior investigators, baseline natural language processing models, and other basic large language models. In an exploratory human-AI collaboration experiment, we found that the collaboration between CoTI and junior investigators provided only marginal gains compared to CoTI alone. A possible hypothesis was that junior investigators may overrely on CoTI and limit their independent critical thinking. Conclusions CoTI can improve the efficiency of thematic analysis by rapidly generating supporting excerpts, initial codes, and themes for human researchers’ review. These findings highlight CoTI’s potential as a useful tool for scalable qualitative research.

Abstract India's vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 rests significantly on harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) to power an inclusive digital economy, with the gig and platform sector projected to grow from 7.7 million workers in 2020-21 to 23.5 million by 2029-30 [1]. Within this expanding workforce lies an under-documented segment: college students who work as ride-hailing drivers and delivery partners for platforms such as Uber, Ola, Rapido, Swiggy, and Zomato alongside their academic commitments. While the Code on Social Security, 2020, operationalised through Rules notified in 2025-26, extends formal welfare recognition to gig and platform workers for the first time, it remains largely silent on the algorithmic mechanisms, dynamic pricing, rating-based deactivation, and automated task allocation, that govern their day-to-day work experience, a gap well documented in the international algorithmic-management literature [2], [3], [4]. This paper examines the intersection of AI-driven algorithmic management and worker welfare policy through a mixed-methods approach: a review of the current regulatory framework combined with primary survey data (n = 18) collected from college students in Coimbatore district engaged in gig work. The findings show that a majority of respondents report unpredictable pricing (70.6%) and roughly two in five report unfair ratings (41.2%) or deactivation/suspension (35.3%), while awareness of the e-Shram portal (52.9%) and of statutory welfare benefits (58.8%, with a further 23.5% only vaguely aware) remains partial. The paper concludes with a policy framework recommending algorithmic transparency mandates, accessible grievance redressal mechanisms, and targeted awareness measures for student and youth gig workers, contributing to the broader goal of inclusive, technology-driven, and socially secure economic growth envisioned under Viksit Bharat @2047.

The integration of behavioral sensing and care technology in dementia care facilities represents a growing operational and strategic priority for care system managers, health system planners, and policymakers confronting the escalating global burden of dementia. Despite substantial and increasing investment in sensing technologies — including motion detection, wearable biosensors, ambient acoustic monitoring, and integrated smart environment platforms — the gap between technology deployment and effective operational integration remains wide, persistent, and insufficiently understood from an organizational and systems analytics perspective (Pappadà et al., 2021). This paper presents an integrative analytical review of the scholarly literature on behavioral sensing and care technology integration in dementia care facilities, organized across five thematic domains: functional architecture and care-relevant capabilities of sensing systems; technology adoption frameworks and evidence patterns in care facility settings; caregiver workflow integration and human factors in technology deployment; organizational readiness, governance, and institutional enablers; and care quality outcomes and decision support implications. The synthesis develops an analytical framework organized around four interdependent implementation dimensions — implementation readiness, workflow alignment, governance and data utilization, and outcome realization — and identifies the conditions under which technology deployment produces sustained operational value and decision-relevant intelligence for care system managers. Principal findings establish that technology integration failure is predominantly organizational rather than technical in origin; that the gap between deployment and deep integration is the most consequential diagnostic distinction in the implementation landscape; and that the decision support function of sensing data — its translation into improved care planning and clinical governance — represents the primary unrealized potential of current technology investment in the dementia care sector. Structured recommendations are advanced for care facility management, health system policy, and future empirical research. The paper is addressed to the health systems and organizational analytics community and contributes a consolidated, decision-relevant framework for understanding and improving technology integration in dementia care contexts.

Intrinsic motivation plays a central role in adaptive and goal-directed behavior by conferring agents reward-independent objectives and biases useful to act in noisy and uncertain environments. Active Inference addresses the problem of acting in a partially observable environment through a principled framework for belief updating and action selection. A key component of Active Inference is the specification of prior preferences, which shapes behavior by encoding desirable future outcomes. An intrinsic motivation approach called the Maximum Occupancy Principle (MOP) proposes that agents act so as to maximize occupancy over future paths of states and actions, with no preferences or epistemic targets. Despite its simple formulation, MOP gives rise to rich and adaptive behaviors that combine exploratory variability with goal-directed dynamics. In this work, we extend MOP to partially observable environments and introduce a Bellman reformulation of the Expected Free Energy for Active Inference, both incorporating belief-based inference over hidden states as part of the agent state. The Bellman formulation enables tractable offline computation via value iteration over the full belief-state space. We compare the resulting behaviors in a set of minimal experimental settings with uncertain food sources. We find that MOP agents switch between goal-directed (food seeking) behavior and exploration between different food sources, depending on their energy available and their belief state. In contrast, Active Inference agents mostly inhabit regions around a single food source, a strategy having both high pragmatic and epistemic value. We finally compare with Empowerment, which is shown to be qualitatively similar to Active Inference.

Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for deployment as the control component of robotic health attendants (RHAs), yet their safety in this context remains poorly characterized. We introduce a dataset of 270 harmful instructions spanning nine prohibited behaviour categories grounded in the American Medical Association (AMA) Principles of Medical Ethics, and use it to evaluate 72 LLMs in a simulation environment based on the RHA framework. The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4%, with more than half exceeding 50%, and violation rates varied substantially across behaviour categories, with superficially plausible instructions such as device manipulation and emergency delay proving harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones. Model size and release date were the primary determinants of safety performance among open-weight models, and proprietary models were substantially safer than open-weight counterparts (median 23.7% versus 72.8%). Medical domain fine-tuning conferred no significant overall safety benefit, and a prompt-based defence strategy produced only a modest reduction in violation rates among the least safe models, leaving violation rates that would preclude safe clinical deployment. These findings demonstrate that safety evaluation must be treated as a first-class criterion in the development and deployment of LLM-based RHAs.

documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hypospadias is a heterogeneous congenital anomaly. This selected narrative review examines emerging domains that may complement conventional surgical care, with particular emphasis on complex, proximal, atypical, familial, or disorder of sex development (DSD)-associated presentations and on long-term outcomes. Methods: A structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted for English-language human or clinically applicable translational literature published from January 2000 through December 2025, supplemented by reference screening and targeted updating of genetics, non-operative management, and adult-outcome literature. Results: Objective phenotyping may improve anatomical description and research comparability. Endocrine/genetic evaluation should be considered in proximal hypospadias, including boys with descended testes, and is most clearly indicated when accompanied by cryptorchidism, micropenis, undervirilisation, familial disease, or other features suggestive of DSD; isolated distal hypospadias without such features does not generally require genetic or formal multidisciplinary DSD assessment. Limited evidence also supports explicit consideration of non-operative management in selected mild distal cases, while studies of uncorrected distal hypospadias report heterogeneous functional and cosmetic outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI), quantitative tissue assessment, registries, and biobanks remain investigational. Long-term studies highlight sexual, reproductive, psychosocial, and late surgical outcomes that may extend into adulthood. As generative AI adopts subscription models, understanding continued payment intentions is essential. Drawing on the expectation-confirmation model, this study integrates technical quality and human–AI relational perceptions to explain continued subscription intention for ChatGPT. Survey data from 565 paid users show that system and information quality affect subscription intention directly and indirectly through expectation confirmation, perceived usefulness, and satisfaction. Satisfaction has the strongest direct effect. Liking and trust influence subscription intention both directly and through satisfaction, whereas intimacy operates mainly through satisfaction. Perceived threat and anxiety have no significant direct or mediated effects. The findings extend the expectation-confirmation model to generative AI subscriptions and identify satisfaction as the central mechanism connecting cognitive evaluations, positive relational perceptions, and continued payment decisions.

documents.abstract: Most academic and nonprofit institutions have mission- and policy-driven mandates to make research data publicly available at no cost to users, however the viability of maintaining “open access,” public collections in the rapidly developing AI ecosystem is uncertain. Since 2022, rising bot traffic associated with large language models and machine learning has cost research collection hosts and maintainers increasing amounts of time, labor, and money. Academic institutions, data hubs, and open collections like Wikipedia all report struggles to minimize downtime and compute costs due to bot confrontations. While defense against bots is an urgent, visceral concern right now, collections managers in these institutions have a particular existential concern: that the bot traffic signifies that entrepreneurial technologists are absorbing generations of curatorial work into systems that may ultimately undermine those collections. This concern is exacerbated by the difficulty in gauging collection “use” (and therefore, value) by traditional website analytics and metrics. What if these challenges, taken together, could also signify opportunities - including mechanisms to encourage better behavior from bots? Our poster will share findings regarding current approaches taken by collection curators. We will then share several new approaches that explicitly work to shift both technical and social incentives in order to address these issues.

documents.abstract: The rapid transformation of the hospitality industry, driven by digitalization, artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and changing guest expectations, requires higher education institutions to continuously align graduate competencies with industry needs. Nevertheless, competency mismatches between hospitality graduates and employer expectations remain a persistent issue, particularly in vocational education. This study aims to identify competency gaps among hospitality graduates, explore priority soft skills required by employers, formulate curriculum improvement recommendations, and examine preferred models of polytechnic–industry collaboration. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed using a Focus Group Discussion (FGD) involving nine corporate managers representing Human Resources, Hotel Operations, Housekeeping, Revenue Management, Information Technology, and Marketing Communication at Ashley Hotel Indonesia. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Four major themes emerged. First, technical competency gaps were identified in operational hotel systems, Property Management Systems (PMS), revenue management, AI utilization, digital marketing, business knowledge, housekeeping procedures, and analytical software. Second, communication, adaptability, critical thinking, problem solving, decision making, observation, and professional attitude were recognized as essential employability skills. Third, curriculum reform should emphasize experiential learning through industry projects, role play, mentoring, AI integration, and competency-based assessment. Finally, respondents highlighted the importance of sustainable polytechnic–industry collaboration through guest lectures, curriculum co-development, internship supervision, practitioner mentoring, and continuous curriculum evaluation. The study proposes an Industry-Based Hospitality Competency Framework integrating technical competencies, employability skills, digital capability, and industry partnership. The findings provide practical implications for curriculum redesign within hospitality higher education to improve graduate employability and workforce readiness.

Abstract : Purpose – This study examines the curriculum–competency gap in hospitality Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Ghana. It considers how curriculum relevance, experiential learning and job competency relate to industry readiness, while also examining what happens to curriculum–industry alignment as occupational and technological requirements change. Design/methodology/approach – The study uses directed qualitative content analysis of 12 purposively selected regulatory, development, institutional, industry and media documents published between 2021 and 2026. The analysis combined theoretically informed coding with comparison across sources, allowing both anticipated relationships and additional patterns in the documentary evidence to be identified. Findings – The evidence shows that curriculum relevance is important for developing competencies that reflect occupational requirements, but relevant content alone does not ensure that graduates are prepared for work. Experiential learning provides opportunities for learners to apply and refine curriculum-based knowledge in workplace settings. Industry readiness consequently depends not only on competency development but also on whether those competencies correspond with what hospitality employers currently require. The analysis also points to a temporal problem: as technologies, work practices and employer expectations change, an initially relevant curriculum may become progressively less aligned with industry requirements if educational adaptation is slow. This pattern informed the concept of curriculum relevance decay, while curriculum adaptability emerged as an institutional response to the problem. Research limitations/implications – The findings are based on documentary evidence and do not provide longitudinal confirmation of curriculum relevance decay. The concept should therefore be treated as a theoretically informed explanation requiring further empirical testing through longitudinal, multi-stakeholder and quantitative research. Practical implications – Maintaining curriculum relevance requires more than periodic curriculum review. Hospitality TVET institutions need continuing engagement with employers, meaningful workplace learning, appropriate technologies and mechanisms for identifying emerging competency requirements before substantial gaps develop.

Abstract India's expansion of higher education has created unprecedented opportunities for young people, yet the movement from educational qualification to meaningful employment remains uneven. The central challenge is no longer simply access to degrees but the relationship between credentials, capabilities, workplace experience, and employment outcomes. This conceptual paper examines how the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 can contribute to narrowing this education–employment gap through the integrated development of AI literacy, communication competence, and work-integrated learning. Drawing on recent policy evidence from NITI Aayog, the International Labour Organization, and contemporary scholarship on artificial intelligence and work-integrated learning, the paper argues that employability should not be treated as an additional soft-skills component appended to an academic curriculum. Rather, it should emerge from a coherent educational architecture connecting disciplinary knowledge with communication, digital and AI capabilities, authentic workplace exposure, critical thinking, and demonstrable competence. The paper proposes an integrated framework in which AI literacy and communication competence function as enabling capabilities, while work-integrated learning provides the context in which those capabilities are tested and developed. It concludes by suggesting institutional measures through which Indian higher education can move from credential-centred education towards competency-, experience-, and outcome-oriented graduate preparation.

documents.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) rely heavily on real-time situational awareness, the quality of which depends directly on the latency and bandwidth of data transmission between the aerial platform and the ground control station. This paper presents a comparative analysis of two UAV communication architectures: conventional radio frequency (RF) links and a system based on a fiber-optic cable deployed during flight. In RF-based systems, visual data transmission is typically performed using compression techniques (e.g., H.264/H.265), which introduce significant delays not only due to encoding and decoding, but also as a result of transmission, buffering, and radio-related processes such as modulation and encryption. Additionally, the limited bandwidth of RF links imposes quality and functional trade-offs, while maintaining low latency requirements for telemetry data. Consequently, certain functions, such as control and data processing, must be executed onboard the UAV, limiting the applicability of advanced image analysis algorithms. In contrast, the use of a fiber-optic link provides very high bandwidth and minimal latency, enabling the transmission of uncompressed video and the offloading of computationally intensive processes, including artificial intelligence algorithms, to the ground station. This allows for centralized processing and improves the accuracy of visual data analysis. The paper compares both architectures in terms of latency, hardware requirements, and implementation costs, while also considering the limitations associated with fiber-optic systems, such as cable mass, mechanical complexity, and reduced system mobility. The results indicate that although fiber-optic solutions offer significant advantages in latency reduction and data quality, their deployment involves substantial structural and operational trade-offs.

Writing anxiety and enjoyment are key affective factors influencing EFL students’ writing development. This study adopted a mixed-methods approach to examine the emotional impact of ChatGPT-generated feedback and online teacher feedback on Indonesian EFL students’ writing anxiety and enjoyment. Fifty undergraduate students were divided into two groups: 26 received automated feedback from ChatGPT, while 24 received teacher feedback via Padlet. Quantitative data were gathered using preand posttests based on the English Writing Anxiety Scale (EWAS) and the English Writing Enjoyment Scale (EWES), along with closed-ended perception questionnaires. Qualitative data were collected through open-ended questionnaire responses to explore students’ perceived effectiveness and affective experiences with the feedback. Quantitative findings showed that both groups experienced nonsignificant reductions in writing anxiety, while only the teacher feedback group reported a significant increase in writing enjoyment. No significant differences were observed between groups in either variable after the intervention. However, perception data revealed that students from both groups viewed the feedback as effective and emotionally positive. Qualitative responses highlighted that ChatGPT feedback was appreciated for its immediacy and technical support, whereas teacher feedback was valued for its contextual relevance and emotional encouragement. These findings underscore the complementary potential of AI and human feedback in enhancing EFL writing instruction and fostering emotionally supportive and pedagogically rich environments by integrating AI-generated and teacher-provided feedback. The study underscores the importance of blending technological tools with human interaction to address both the cognitive and affective needs of language learners.

documents.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) utilization as a teaching assistant on teachers’ workload and the quality of educational interactions in Islamic schools (Madrasahs). Employing a mixed-methods sequential explanatory design, the study involved 120 teachers divided into an experimental group (AI users) and a control group. Quantitative findings revealed a significant reduction in the workload of teachers using AI (Δ = -18.5 points, p < 0.001) and a significant improvement in the quality of educational interactions (Δ = +1.4 points, p < 0.001). Furthermore, a strong correlation was found between the reduction in time-related workload and the enhancement of a positive classroom climate (r = -0.72). Qualitative findings indicated that the time saved through AI assistance (16.8 hours per week) was reallocated to personal interactions with students and character development activities. The study confirms that AI has the potential to transform the teacher’s role from mu'allim (knowledge transmitter) to murabbi (character educator), provided that its implementation is managed wisely and ethically.

Autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents deployed on extended software engineering, research, and planning tasks require persistent long-term memory across sessions. Existing agent architectures predominantly rely on traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paradigms that partition documents into arbitrary, fixed-window character or token chunks stored in append-only vector databases. In long-running autonomous workflows, this approach exhibits three fatal pathologies:1. **Semantic Fragmentation**: Fixed-width token slicing arbitrarily splits interdependent entities, preconditions, and constraints across chunk boundaries, causing context omission and multi-hop reasoning failure.2. **Append-Only Memory Bloat**: Every agent turn indiscriminately writes redundant observations to the vector store, producing unbounded $O(N)$ index explosion, increased retrieval latency, and context poisoning.3. **Black-Box Opacity**: Embedding-only vector stores cannot be audited, inspected, diffed, or corrected by human engineers via standard version-control workflows. We introduce **Capsule**, an open-source, dual-plane memory architecture specifically designed for autonomous agents. Capsule enforces an *atomic fact representation* ("one self-contained fact per Markdown file") stored with structured YAML frontmatter directly on the filesystem (the *Storage Plane*), while maintaining high-speed derived indexes (SQLite FTS5 / PostgreSQL `tsvector` + vector embeddings) in an ephemeral, rebuildable database (the *Retrieval Plane*). Capsule introduces:- **Normalized SHA-256 Content-Hash Deduplication**: Intercepts redundant observations, merging updates into idempotent canonical nodes with tracked revision lineages.- **Token-Bounded Knapsack Context Composition**: Replaces blind top-$k$ chunk concatenation with a budget-constrained optimization problem that packs maximal information density into the prompt window. We rigorously evaluate Capsule against standard fixed-window RAG across four empirical benchmarks:- **Retrieval Efficiency**: Capsule achieves a **36.9% reduction in prompt token consumption** while improving multi-hop fact recall from **93.3% to 100.0%**, and more than doubling context information density from **34.1% to 71.4%**.- **Downstream Reasoning**: In an end-to-end evaluation using a frontier LLM (`Gemini 2.5 Flash`), Capsule increases multi-hop architectural question answering accuracy from **50.0% to 93.3% (+43.3% absolute improvement)** while slashing input token costs by **37.3%**.- **Multi-Turn Memory Bloat Simulation**: Over an extended 50-step iterative agent task, Capsule prunes **85.0% of redundant submissions**, bounding long-term memory growth and reducing token storage footprint by **51.8%** compared to traditional append-only vector stores.- **Component Ablations**: We isolate the contributions of hybrid retrieval, knapsack budget packing, and content deduplication, demonstrating that removing any single component causes steep degradation in token efficiency or context precision. Capsule is released as an open-source package (`pip install kapsule`) with native CLI utilities, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and automated daemon harvesters.

The COVID-19 pandemic intensified existing inequalities among vulnerable populations, particularly where multiple factors, such as gender, age, nationality, and socioeconomic status, intersected. For these groups, one critical yet underexplored dimension of the crisis was informational: many faced uncertainty in accessing essential services and navigating daily life. Public policies often failed to address these challenges adequately, leaving civil society actors (CSAs), including NGOs, associations, and informal groups, to fill the gap, frequently through the use of information and communication technologies (ICTs). This article investigates how CSAs across Europe employed ICTs to support vulnerable groups during the pandemic. Drawing on data from nearly 300 initiatives mapped by the EU-funded RESISTIRÉ project, we apply the lens of care and telecare practices from Science and Technology Studies (STS) to analyse these responses. Our findings, based on a reflexive thematic analysis, suggest a diverse range of sociotechnical assemblages, from helplines and educational platforms to lobbying campaigns and mutual aid networks. ICTs were used not only to deliver remote health-related support but also to address emotional, educational, and structural needs. These practices varied in their level of user involvement and often relied on familiar technologies to reach digitally excluded populations. By highlighting bottom-up telecare practices, this study contributes to expanding the scope of crisis informatics and telecare research towards intersectional “matters of care” concerning vulnerable populations, emphasizing the role of CSAs and ICTs in shaping inclusive responses to information uncertainty during emergencies.

International experiences provide valuable insights into how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is being explored and integrated within different educational systems. Countries have adopted different approaches according to their educational priorities, technological infrastructure, policies, economic conditions, cultural contexts, and national strategies. This chapter examines selected international case studies from the United States, Finland, Singapore, China, India, and the United Kingdom. These cases provide a comparative perspective on AI-supported teaching, learning, research, educational administration, teacher development, and digital transformation.

Background. The rapid global adoption of ChatGPT has raised growing interest in its role in supporting student learning, yet the effectiveness of generative AI tools in enhancing higher-order cognitive skills such as problem-solving may depend on individual learner characteristics that remain underexplored. Purpose. This quantitative study aimed to examine the relationship between ChatGPT usage and problem-solving ability among students enrolled in a Media Design course, and to test whether this relationship is moderated by achievement motivation. Method. The study involved 115 university students from four intact classes across two higher education institutions in Thailand and Cambodia. Data were collected through a survey questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), preceded by a measurement invariance test (MICOM) to assess the appropriateness of pooling data across the two national samples. Results. The findings indicate that ChatGPT usage was positively and significantly associated with problem-solving ability (? = 0.386, p < 0.001), as was achievement motivation (? = 0.291, p < 0.01). The interaction between ChatGPT usage and achievement motivation also showed a significant positive effect (? = 0.157, p < 0.05), indicating that achievement motivation strengthens the relationship between ChatGPT usage and problem-solving ability. The model explained 44.6% of the variance in problem-solving ability (R² = 0.446). Conclusion. This study has significant implications for instructional practices in higher education settings, particularly for lecturers designing AI-integrated learning activities. By understanding how achievement motivation shapes students’ benefit from ChatGPT, educators can tailor instructional strategies that support both technology adoption and the development of independent problem solving skills.

documents.abstract: Introduction: Climate change affects health systems in multifaceted ways; particularly, it introduces new areas of responsibility within primary health care services. This study aims to systematically examine scientific publications that address the health impacts of climate change from a primary care perspective, identify thematic trends, and reveal existing gaps.Methods: In this systematic review, conducted in line with PRISMA 2020 principles, publications from 2020 to 2025 containing themes related to primary health care services were examined. Following a comprehensive search in the Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases, 76 publications that met the inclusion criteria were analyzed. The studies were thematically classified and their distribution by year was assessed. Relevance, content, and accessibility filters were operationally predefined to ensure methodological transparency and to standardize study selection based on primary care applicability, eligibility criteria, and full-text availability.Results: The most frequently discussed themes among the reviewed publications were infectious diseases (n=15), general public health impacts (n=18), and mental health (n=12). A more limited number of studies were found in areas such as women's health, health systems, socioeconomic inequalities, and occupational health. A noticeable increase in the number of publications was observed in 2023 and 2024; however, studies specifically focusing on primary care services remain limited within the current literature.Conclusion: This review demonstrates the need to address the health effects of climate change through comprehensive approaches at the primary care level. Primary health care services occupy a strategic position in terms of preventive practices, early diagnosis, and reaching vulnerable groups. However, the existing literature reveals a lack of focused studies in this context. The findings point to a need for more research on policy development and implementation models specific to primary care in order to build health systems resilient to the climate crisis. Strengthening evidence-based approaches in primary care is essential for climate-resilient and sustainable health systems.

Shade selection for tooth restoration is a crucial step in achieving patient satisfaction in aesthetic dentistry. The practitioner should know the aspects of color, as well as the illumination of the object, the teeth and their surroundings and the observer himself. Given the highly subjective nature of the process, conventional shade guides were developed, along with modernized shade-taking devices, to achieve excellent color-matched restorations. Nevertheless, determining the correct shade of the restoration remains a significant challenge in routine dental practice. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to improve the efficiency of shade matching. However, the clinical impact of its implementation and the limitations it poses remain inadequately explored. We conducted a systematic review, searching PubMed, ScienceDirect and Cochrane Library for studies. Eligible studies reported outcomes on AI performance compared with traditional triage methods. Risk of bias was assessed. The included studies (n=11) demonstrated AI’s potential to reduce triage time, improve accuracy and enhance decision support. However, limitations included under-triage risks, variable accuracy and predominance of single-center studies. In addition to implementation challenges, including workflow integration barriers and clinician acceptance. The use of AI models in esthetic dentistry improved accuracy in shade selection and restoration color prediction compared with conventional visual methods. Nevertheless, given the variability in results and the predominance of laboratory-based and single-center validation studies, large-scale clinical validation studies and standardized outcome reporting are required to synthesize evidence on long-term impact, patient-related esthetic outcomes and ethical considerations regarding the routine use of AI models.

The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into educational research is reshaping core practices such as literature reviews and qualitative analysis. However, this methodological transition creates tension between gains in operational efficiency and the latent risk of erosion of higher-order cognitive competencies. Existing scholarship suggests that productive GenAI integration requires the deliberate exercise of these competencies to preserve the researcher's intellectual agency. Despite this, their monitoring remains underexplored. This study examines how researchers draw on three fundamental cognitive competencies (abstract, systemic, and analytical thinking) when using the MIXAI workflow in GenAI-supported methodological literature reviews. Methodologically, an embedded single case study design was adopted, with the MIXAI workflow as the instrumental case and six researchers in training as the units of analysis. The corpus of 22 reflective diary-portfolios was analyzed using the Framework Analysis Method through hybrid human–AI coding and structured cross-validation under strict human epistemic control. The results show that the five dimensions of the Abstract–Systemic–Analytical–Reflective–Integrative (ASARI) model are activated differentially: analytical thinking functions as an entry-level competence driven by workflow structure; abstract thinking is unlocked by overcoming technical barriers; and integration depends on prior disciplinary expertise. Seven emerging categories were incorporated as subdimensions, and epistemic coconstruction was identified as a frontier yet to be characterized. The productive exercise (rather than erosion) of cognitive competencies appears less dependent on technical expertise than on the presence of the regulatory dimensions, reflexivity and integration, which keep the researcher as the central epistemic authority. The model provides a framework for monitoring the conditions of GenAI collaboration, while supporting analytical rigor and the central role of human judgment in scientific knowledge production.

documents.abstract: As software engineering rapidly evolves, developers are increasingly tasked with orchestrating complex workflows that combine artificial intelligence architectures and domain-specific data pipelines. This paradigm shift introduces unprecedented cognitive demands, rendering traditional physical ergonomics insufficient. Neuroergonomics—the intersection of neuroscience, human factors, and computing—offers objective methodologies for measuring and mitigating cognitive overload. This paper reviews the application of neuroergonomic principles specifically within modern Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) like Visual Studio Code, focusing on two high-complexity domains: Agentic Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks and structural bioinformatics pipelines. Tasks such as managing state memory in LangGraph, optimizing LLM routing with Phidata, and processing high-dimensional protein structures using AlphaFold DB and FPocket require continuous attentional allocation and complex decision-making. By analyzing real-time neural monitoring (EEG, fNIRS) and eye-tracking studies, this review synthesizes strategies for designing adaptive computing environments. The integration of AI-driven adaptive interfaces that dynamically adjust cognitive load—by modulating notification frequency, summarizing pre-computed pLDDT scores, or streamlining visual layouts—demonstrates significant potential to enhance developer productivity, task accuracy, and long-term cognitive well-being. Ultimately, embedding physiological awareness into AI-assisted development tools represents a transformative leap toward sustainable, human centered software engineering. The orchestration of multi-agent systems introduces unique cognitive bottlenecks not present in traditional sequential programming. Frameworks such as LangGraph and Phidata require developers to conceptualize non-linear state transitions and dynamic memory routing. This architectural complexity forces the human operator to retain massive amounts of temporary information regarding agent states, context windows, and vector retrieval parameters. When an error occurs in these decentralized environments, debugging is no longer a matter of tracing a single linear stack trace, but rather deciphering autonomous agent logic. This specific layer of abstraction inherently spikes extraneous cognitive load, exposing the limitations of conventional, static coding interfaces. Similarly, the integration of structural biology into computational workflows presents intense visual and analytical challenges. Processing high-dimensional datasets from AlphaFold DB and executing pocket detection algorithms via FPocket demands sustained attentional focus. Researchers must frequently cross-reference 3D protein models with dense numerical outputs, relying heavily on metrics like pLDDT confidence scores to make critical design decisions. The visual density of these tasks rapidly depletes cognitive reserves. By applying neuroergonomic principles, next-generation computing environments can be designed to dynamically filter out low-confidence protein regions or suppress non-essential background processes during peak workload, thereby optimizing the user's visual field and preventing premature mental fatigue.

Medical AI interfaces can shape physicians’ agency, diagnostic behavior, and responsibility judgments. In a 2 × 2 within-subjects experiment, 60 radiologists interacted with prescriptive or dialectical interfaces featuring instrumental or placebo controls. We assessed explicit agency, intentional binding, rejection of erroneous AI recommendations, and responsibility allocation, supplemented by interviews. Placebo control was associated with high explicit agency but attenuated intentional binding. In the prescriptive-placebo condition, physicians attributed 62.0% of responsibility to themselves. Dialectical interaction increased rejection of erroneous AI recommendations from 31.8% to 70.3%. These findings show condition-dependent differences in agency measures, diagnostic decisions, and responsibility attribution. Because functional control and feedback predictability varied together, the cause of attenuated intentional binding remains uncertain. Intentional binding and responsibility attribution were analyzed separately; their co-occurrence does not establish mediation. The results support further testing of how interface design affects control and accountability in medical AI.

documents.abstract: Executive summary Cognitive security should protect not only individual humans or individual AI models, but also the interfaces through which cognitive systems exchange representations, assumptions, memory, provenance, constraints, and decision authority. A visible AI failure is often an incorrect answer. A deeper failure can occur when every component remains locally plausible while the larger cognitive system becomes globally incoherent. In complex artificial systems, independently updated modules may remain individually functional while drifting out of alignment. In sustained Human-AI interaction, both participants may remain individually capable while their shared epistemic process progressively loses version integrity, provenance, role separation, or external validation. The security object is therefore not always a component. Sometimes the security object is the relation. Such relational failures can arise accidentally, but they can also be induced. An adversary does not need to compromise any single model, module, or person if it can degrade the relation between them. This contribution proposes coherence governance as a distinct cognitive-security control applicable to both artificial cognitive architectures and Human-AI hybrid systems. Its central rule is simple: coherence should be observable and governable, but it must never be confused with truth, agreement, confidence, or task performance.

Background/objectives: Robotic surgery has experienced rapid growth across multiple surgical specialties over the last two decades, with the da Vinci Surgical System emerging as a dominant global platform. Although robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) offers several technological advantages, including improved ergonomics, precision, and minimally invasive access, its widespread adoption remains constrained by high acquisition, maintenance, and consumable costs. Recently, new robotic platforms have entered the market with the aim of improving economic sustainability while maintaining comparable clinical outcomes. This study aimed to perform a comparative economic evaluation of three robotic surgical platforms currently used at ASST Grande Ospedale Metropolitano Niguarda Hospital, Milano, Italy: Da Vinci, Hugo™ RAS, and Versius®. Methods: Cost-minimization analysis (CMA), break-even analysis (BEA), and one-way deterministic sensitivity analysis (DSA) were conducted. Radical prostatectomy was selected as the reference procedure because of its high institutional volume and availability of published evidence. Cost estimates were derived from a combination of institutional real-world data and literature sources, including fixed costs (equipment acquisition and maintenance) and variable costs (robotic kits, operating room utilization, personnel, and hospitalization). Sensitivity analyses were performed by varying key cost drivers to assess their impact on economic sustainability. Results: Under the assumption of clinical equivalence among platforms, Hugo™ RAS demonstrated the lowest overall per-procedure cost (Euros [€]6,991.26), followed by Da Vinci (€7,839.51) and Versius® (€8,424.97). BEA showed that Hugo™ achieved cost recovery at approximately 124 procedures per year, compared with 161 procedures for Da Vinci and 208 procedures for Versius®. DSA identified the cost of the robotic kit, operative time, and hospitalization duration as the principal determinants of break-even variability across all platforms. Conclusions: Within the evaluated setting, Hugo™ RAS emerged as the most cost-efficient and economically sustainable robotic platform for radical prostatectomy. The findings highlight the importance of consumable costs, operative efficiency, and hospitalization management in determining the financial sustainability of robotic surgery programs. By integrating real-world evidence with economic modeling, this study provides useful information to support hospital decision makers in adopting and managing robotic surgical technologies.

Purpose: Accurate assessment of aortic landing zones (LZs) is essential for planning thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). Manual measurements, while the clinical standard, are time-consuming and prone to inter-operator variability. This study evaluates the reliability of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based tool for standardized LZ assessment. Material and Methods: A retrospective clinical data set of 35 patients was analysed using manual and an AI-assisted methods for evaluating key geometric parameters relevant to TEVAR planning: diameters at the endpoints of the proximal and distal aneurysm (P0, D0) and at the ends of the LZs (P2, D2), conicity indices (TR P , TR D ), and lengths (L PLZ , L DLZ ) of the proximal and distal LZs. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). The data set was stratified according to the anatomical zones of Ishimaru (Group A = 0, 1, and 2 and Group B = 3) to evaluate the influence of the anatomical location of the PLZ on the evaluation and the concordance of the method. Results: Artificial intelligence–assisted and manual measurements showed strong agreement, with ICC values consistently >0.75. No significant differences were observed in TR D between groups (2.2% vs 3.5%, P = .691). However, TR P showed a trend towards higher proximal conicity in Group A vs Group B (−10.6% vs 0.8%, P = .086), with reduced agreement in Group B (ICC = 0.62). Conclusions: Artificial intelligence–assisted methods showed high concordance with manual measurements for most aortic LZ parameters. However, anatomical complexity, especially near zone 0, can affect agreement, particularly in evaluating aortic neck conicity. These findings highlight the importance of considering anatomical variability when validating AI-assisted tools for clinical planning. Clinical Impact This study shows that AI-assisted, centreline-based assessment of aortic landing zones can be integrated into routine TEVAR planning, providing diameters, lengths and conicity indices that agree closely with manual measurements while reducing operator dependency and post-processing time. For clinicians, this translates into faster, standardised and reproducible sizing, less variability between observers and centres, and better-supported decisions on endograft oversizing. The innovation lies in coupling deep-learning segmentation with automated detection of the maximum-area cross-section and of a fixed 25 mm sealing zone along the inner curvature. The reduced agreement observed in anatomically complex arch zones indicates where expert review remains indispensable.

This paper compares the effectiveness of selected publicly available tools for detecting AI-generated text: GPTZero AI Detector, ZeroGPT AI Detector, Copyleaks AI Detector, and Scribbr AI Detector. The experiment included 150 text samples in Polish and English, divided into human-written texts, AI-generated texts, and texts paraphrased using AI. ZeroGPT achieved the highest overall accuracy, equal to 64.0%, and the highest F1-score, equal to 77.7%. GPTZero achieved an accuracy of 58.7%, while Scribbr and Copyleaks achieved lower results, equal to 44.0% and 42.7%, respectively. Fully AI-generated texts were detected more effectively than AI-paraphrased texts. The overall accuracy was similar for Polish and English samples, equal to 52.7% and 52.0%, respectively.

documents.abstract: This article is devoted to the comprehensive evaluation of the design and quality parameters of products made from recycled denim fabric. The relevance of the study is обусловлена increasing interest in sustainable development and the rational use of textile waste in the modern light industry. The study examines clothing, accessories, and interior items created from secondary raw materials obtained from production waste and post-consumer denim materials. Various design solutions were applied in the development of the samples, including patchwork techniques, appliqué, and the use of fibrous filling materials. The evaluation of the samples was carried out based on a set of indicators including strength characteristics, the ability of the material to retain its shape, wear resistance, aesthetic properties, and ergonomic parameters. The analysis was performed using standardized testing methods and comparative analysis. The results showed that the use of recycled denim raw materials up to 50% in the material composition does not lead to a significant deterioration of the main quality indicators of the products. On the contrary, the use of creative design solutions increases the aesthetic attractiveness of the products. In general, it was found that products made from recycled denim have sufficient performance characteristics and can successfully compete in the modern market of environmentally oriented textile products.

This chapter examines how computer-assisted analytical techniques have enabled scholars to ask new questions of text-based cultural materials, framing the tension between computational and traditional modes of reading as a false opposition. The chapter introduces distant reading as a broad spectrum of methods, from basic word frequency analysis to advanced natural language processing and machine learning, and explains how these approaches complement rather than replace close reading. It surveys major tools and methods used in computational text analysis, discussing landmark studies by scholars such as Matthew Jockers and Ted Underwood. The chapter also looks ahead to the impact of large language models on the future of computation for criticism, considering how artificial intelligence may reshape the relationship between quantitative evidence and humanistic interpretation.

The rise of artificial intelligence technologies and their increasing reliance in numerous fields, most notably medicine, is significant. AI plays a crucial role in assisting physicians with accurate patient diagnosis, enabling them to make informed decisions. This article presents a method for integrating computer vision technologies into the medical field, where multimodal medical imaging integrates structural and textual information to support clinical decision-making. However, most image fusion frameworks based on transformers remain narrowly designed for a single media combination and a single subsequent task. This paper proposes the Multimodal Adaptive Fusion Transformer (CMAFT), a unified architecture that combines Swin transformer encoders for each media with a Catalyst Cross Attention Fusion Module (GCAF) to dynamically weight each media's contribution based on its real-time reliability. CMAFT was evaluated against two structurally different multimodal reference standards: the BraTS 2021 dataset, in which four MRI sequences (T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR) were combined to segment brain tumor volumes, and the MIMIC-CXR dataset, in which chest X-ray images were combined with duplex radiology report inclusions to classify multimodal pathology and generate reports. The proposed GCAF module provides a learnable reliability gateway that curbs degraded or lost data streams, while a multiscale hierarchical integration pyramid preserves both fine detail and overall semantic context. Experiments show that CMAFT achieves average Dice scores of 92.4%, 87.9%, and 84.6% for whole tumor, tumor nucleus, and enhanced tumor, respectively, on the BraTS 2021 dataset, and a multi-class average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876 with an overall F1 value of 0.658 on the MIMIC-CXR dataset, outperforming modern hybrid CNN-Transformer models while using fewer parameters compared to similar dual-code baseline models. Resection studies confirm that both reliability gate and multi-scale integration contribute to measurable gains, and that CMAFT degrades smoothly when either an MRI sequence or radiology report is unavailable. These results suggest that a single adaptive mutual attention integration design can be generalized across volumetric and text-based multimodal diagnostic pathways.
