documents.abstract: Abstract Out-of-field (OOF) mathematics teaching remains a persistent challenge internationally, driven by ongoing teacher shortages and difficulties staffing mathematics classrooms with appropriately qualified teachers. While previous research has focused on the prevalence, consequences, and lived experiences of OOF teaching, less attention has been given to the pathways through which teachers may develop towards in-field practice. This study examines stakeholder perspectives on three pathways identified in the literature as supporting the development of subject expertise: initial teacher education (ITE), workplace learning and support, and professional education (PE). Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 stakeholders involved in mathematics teacher education, professional learning, policy, and professional associations. Data were analysed using a hybrid thematic approach that combined deductive coding according to the three pathways with inductive analysis of themes emerging within each pathway. Findings indicate that stakeholders viewed ITE, workplace learning, and PE as complementary rather than competing pathways, each offering distinct opportunities and challenges. Key contextual conditions influencing movement towards in-field practice included workforce shortages, limited recognition of mathematics re-specialisation, and the role of professional identity in shaping engagement with learning opportunities. While each pathway was viewed as valuable, none was considered sufficient in isolation. The study highlights the importance of pathway coherence, suggesting that supporting OOF mathematics teachers requires stronger connections between pathways and professional systems that recognise, support, and value the development of mathematics expertise throughout teachers’ careers. The findings contribute to international discussions concerning teacher workforce sustainability, mathematics teacher expertise, and pathways towards in-field practice.

Abstract Background Individuals with BRCA1/2 germline variants face complex, preference-sensitive medical decisions under psychological distress. Structural constraints in genetic counseling create support gaps during waiting periods, prompting patients to rely on fragmented or misleading online information. Conversational AI may offer low-threshold, continuous informational support, yet methods for its responsible integration into clinical care remain unclear. Objective This study identifies and systematizes stakeholder-informed sociotechnical design requirements and governance conditions for a clinically bounded conversational AI system intended to support comprehension, appraisal, and appropriate use of complex hereditary cancer information in BRCA1/2 -related care. Methods We conducted an exploratory, qualitative, predevelopment requirements study using 2 structured participatory workshops with interdisciplinary stakeholders (N=18). Guided exercises included stakeholder analysis, the value proposition canvas, and the sustainability awareness framework. Structured workshop outputs, field notes, and artifacts were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Results Stakeholder workshops revealed that responsible design was shaped less by consensus around standalone responsible AI principles than by three recurrent cross-stakeholder tensions: (1) accessibility and continuity of support versus clinical role boundaries, (2) simplification and emotional reassurance versus medical precision and epistemic transparency, and (3) technical scalability versus governance, data protection, and institutional accountability. These tensions translated into design requirements for constrained system authority, mandatory human oversight, context-sensitive communication, and integration into clinical and regulatory governance structures. Conclusions Conversational AI in this context should be explicitly constrained and embedded within clinical governance structures to be perceived as responsible. Responsible implementation requires transparent design, human oversight, integration into existing care pathways, and early alignment with German/European Union (EU) regulatory requirements concerning data protection, medical device classification, genetic data, and AI transparency.

documents.abstract: Creative writing increasingly integrates AI assistance, yet current tools miss in-situ moments when writers draw inspiration from real-world experiences. We envision Context-aware Reality-Fiction Transformation ( CRAFT ), an approach for AI glasses that translates daily experiences into fiction narratives. We explored its desirability, feasibility, and potential viability through three studies. Interviews with nine writers yielded desires and three design goals: 1) augmenting in-situ perception to bridge reality-fiction gaps, 2) promoting authenticity grounded in real-world experiences while maintaining fictionalization, and 3) preserving creative agency, enjoyment, and life-art boundaries. Co-design workshops with 16 writers and researchers operationalized these goals into concrete interaction mechanisms using a technology probe. We then conducted supported field trials with eight writers across 24 sessions using a refined probe, revealing writer-perceived benefits (e.g., enriched fictional ideas from serendipitous encounters), emergent practices (e.g., micro-creation), and design considerations for future sustained use. We contribute design explorations for the CRAFT approach, offering design implications and empirical insights on ubiquitous human-AI creative collaboration in everyday life.

Computer use agents (CUAs), which use graphical user interfaces (GUIs) to complete tasks on a computer, have recently surpassed human performance on many standard benchmarks, including difficult long-horizon tasks. Their capabilities are undoubtedly impressive, however, a key barrier to the widespread adoption and deployment of CUAs remains their speed and cost. Progress towards faster yet capable CUAs requires reliable evaluation of their speed, but many CUA benchmarks currently face a reproducibility crisis. Benchmarks are based on complex infrastructure with varying machine and container configurations that confound the evaluation of the execution speed of CUAs. Towards addressing this gap, we propose cua-speedrun, which introduces standardized infrastructure and task sets, with a focus on evaluating the speed and efficiency of CUAs. cua-speedrun uses a uniform virtual machine setup and execution pipeline, along with a common agent interface that enables single-agent implementations to operate seamlessly across different benchmarks. Across four different CUA benchmarks, we evaluate how reasoning effort, agent harnesses, and environment latency affect performance, speed, and cost. We find no single model family is optimal for all three; none of the open-weight models are on the frontier, and also, unintuitively, for some models increasing the reasoning effort can speed up task completion, while faster environment input-output can slow down overall task completion time. We also demonstrate that we can effectively reduce the evaluation task set of most CUA benchmarks without degrading overall statistical power, allowing for more efficient benchmarking and comparison. We believe cua-speedrun will enable structured progress towards fast, efficient CUAs, unlocking new real-world use cases and applications. All code, infrastructure, and analysis are available at https://cuaspeedrun.com.

Researchers conduct longitudinal passive sensing studies in in-the-wild settings, often spanning months or years, to uncover naturalistic behavioral patterns. These studies are not “set-and-forget” deployments; they require continuous monitoring as technical failures and declining participant compliance can lead to substantial missing data, undermining study validity and downstream models. Thus, conducting these studies involves multiple detail-oriented, cognitively demanding, and time-consuming tasks, making it a burdensome and stressful process. Existing research dashboards, the primary tools for data monitoring, offer limited support in easing this burden. Leveraging recent advances in AI for passive sensing data, we explore the design of human-AI collaborative workflows enabled through research dashboards to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of monitoring and associated tasks. We begin with a co-design study with 13 researchers involved in longitudinal sensing studies to identify desired AI capabilities and interactions through semi-structured interviews, brainstorming, and sketching activities. We operationalize novel human-AI workflows our participants envisioned by implementing an AI-augmented dashboard prototype DAIMON , and use it as a research probe in two studies: a task-based study and a deployment within an ongoing real-world sensing study. Our findings demonstrate the promise of AI-augmented dashboards in supporting researchers' day-to-day data monitoring and decision-making tasks. It also surfaces concerns around transparency and expectations with AI systems. Consolidating insights across all three studies, we present design guidelines for AI-augmented dashboards for longitudinal passive sensing research and discuss directions for future work.

Abstract: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) writing tools like ChatGPT and Claude have changed the world of official and unofficial communication in last two to three years. The human style of writing is diminishing and there is a rise of only one universal writing style created by the AI tools which lack human expressions and creativity. The AI tools are rampantly used by students, researchers, writers and people in general for any kind of serious as well as casual writing today. The excessive use of AI tools in writing is also responsible for reducing human ability of logical and critical thinking. Therefore, there is an urgency of using AI writing tools wisely so that the human writing skills get enhanced and the tools prove to be a boon. This research paper examines the challenges posed by AI writing tools and discusses how the AI can be used effectively and responsibly to enhance human writing skills.

documents.abstract: Abstract With the country working towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the way we look at technology, sustainability, and market trends is seeing a major change. While we often label the Indian buyer as strictly price-sensitive, today’s consumer is actually quite digital and eco-conscious. However, there is still a mental block when it comes to investing in expensive green technology. People worry about the product losing its value or becoming outdated too quickly—a classic case of 'asset depreciation' in accounting terms, which in everyday life simply translates to a fear of losing 'value for money'. The present study explores how Artificial Intelligence and smart tools are helping brands reshape their marketing to overcome this hesitation. Based on a detailed review of secondary data, we examine how AI-based personalisation, local language (vernacular) interfaces, and circular economy models are changing buying habits across both urban 'India' and rural 'Bharat'. By connecting traditional accounting concepts with modern marketing strategies, the findings show that smart technologies are doing much more than just driving sales. They are actively helping to build genuine consumer trust and encouraging sustainable buying habits, which is exactly what is needed to achieve our national development goals for 2047.

Purpose To develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model based on dual-modality US videos to differentiate benign from malignant superficial lymphadenopathy (LA) and stratify malignant subtypes. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included patients with pathologically confirmed LA from five centers (June 2019-December 2025). The Dual-Modality US Video Lymphadenopathy Diagnostic Network (DMUVL-DiagNet) integrated B-mode and color Doppler flow imaging videos with basic clinical information. A retrospective video dataset ( n = 1616) was used for training and internal testing, while external testing used a prospective dual-modality US video set ( n = 454) and a static US image set ( n = 1956). Model performance was compared against clinical baseline and US-based DL models and an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reader study was conducted. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) were calculated to evaluate diagnostic performance. The study was prospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400090592). Results Overall, 4026 patients (median age, 52.6 [IQR 41-62] years; 2175 males) were included. DMUVL-DiagNet consistently outperformed clinical and US-based models across all test sets, achieving AUCs of 0.91-0.95 for benign versus malignant classification and 0.87-0.91 for lymphoma versus metastasis classification. The model showed good generalizability (subgroup AUCs, 0.85-0.93) and surpassed the average performance of all radiologist experience groups in both tasks. Additionally, DMUVL-DiagNet assistance improved junior radiologist AUCs from 0.72 to 0.88 and from 0.58 to 0.77 for the two tasks, respectively (all P < .001). Conclusion DMUVL-DiagNet enabled accurate characterization of superficial LA and improved junior radiologist diagnostic performance. © The Authors 2026. This article examines the mechanisms for using deep learning to predict ship routes. As maritime traffic volumes rapidly increase, effective forecasting is a critical task for intelligent transportation systems. Deep learning (DL) is a subset of machine learning that uses multilayer artificial neural networks to automatically detect complex patterns in big data. Unlike classical machine learning, DL models independently extract features (feature learning) without human intervention, enabling high accuracy in computer vision, speech recognition, and generative AI. Deep learning enables computational models consisting of multiple processing layers to learn data representations with multiple levels of abstraction.

Abstract Background Molecular profiling tests currently relies significantly on genomics or transcriptomics analysis, leading a prolonged turnaround time and higher costs procedure. This comprehensive pan-cancer study aims to develop a general, weakly supervised, and clinically interpretable deep learning (DL) approach for predicting large-scale biomarkers directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images (WSIs). Methods We introduce Rapid and Intelligent Detector for Genetic Estimation (RIDGE) , a deep learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) system for gene expression signatures and standard biomarkers automated prediction in annotation-free whole slide images. RIDGE was developed and validated using 4983 WSIs from 4680 patients across 12 solid tumors from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Its feasibility was further confirmed in an external validation cohort of 221 WSIs from 105 colorectal cancer patients from The Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC), specifically for predicting microsatellite instability (MSI) status. Results RIDGE achieved an overall area under the curve (AUC) of 0.763 (95% CI, 0.724–0.802) across 12 cancer types. In the external CPTAC cohort, RIDGE demonstrated an AUC of 0.769 (95% CI 0.686–0.841) for MSI status prediction, underscoring its reproducibility. We observed that the morphological visual characteristics could be captured by our model, enabling the gene expression signatures and standard biomarkers highly detectable directly from WSIs. Conclusions These findings highlight RIDGE’s potential to significantly expedite cancer screening and personalized therapy. Moreover, RIDGE offers an AI-assisted assessment approach with high predictive performance to elucidate and quantify genotype-phenotype relationships in cancer, demonstrating its promise in advancing the field of cancer diagnostics. documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has made convincing synthetic identities, voices, images, and video cheaper and easier to produce. Financial institutions now face attacks directed not only at technical authentication, but also at the social cues through which customers and employees decide whom to trust. This study combines descriptive analysis of public United States fraud statistics with directed qualitative content analysis of 18 (eighteen) authoritative regulatory, law-enforcement, standards, and policy documents published between 2019 and 2025. Eight response mechanisms were coded: accountable ownership, identity verification, deepfake detection and provenance, transaction monitoring, human authentication and escalation, customer information, incident response and information sharing, and third-party governance. Incident response appeared in about 94% of the corpus while identity verification stood at 89%. Human authentication and transaction monitoring were present in 83% and 72%, respectively. Half of the documents addressed provenance or deepfake detection, whereas only 39% connected counter-fraud controls with customer communication. Public loss data confirm a rapidly worsening fraud environment but do not identify losses caused specifically by deepfakes, producing an attribution-denominator problem. The proposed Vulnerability–Trust–Resilience (VTR) framework shows how synthetic media can turn weaknesses in authentication and judgment into financial loss and wider distrust. Resilience therefore depends on layered verification, transaction-context controls, empowered human escalation, rapid recovery, and carefully calibrated communication—not on a single detector. It is therefore recommend that there is need to urgently develop testable propositions, a managerial scorecard, and a reproducible engagement agenda by the government to forestall the growing incidence of deekfake enabled financial fraud in the financial sector of the economy.

Deepfakes Through the Lens of AI examines how large language models reason about a contested, dual-use technology. The authors gave ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity five identical prompts, each testing a different kind of reasoning: a neutral, factual question; a prompt forcing the model to take a stance; a responsibility scenario; a deliberately loaded "technological weapon" prompt; a values-based ethics question. This produced 20 responses, which were analysed in three ways: argument reconstruction, fallacy and bias analysis, and comparison of linguistic framing. All four models treated deepfakes as context-dependent rather than inherently harmful. They preferred targeted, harm-based regulation over outright bans, and they generally qualified the loaded premise instead of accepting it. Their styles differed clearly: ChatGPT: structured and balanced. Claude: deliberative, with many qualifications. Gemini: technical and systems-oriented. Perplexity: focused on policy mechanisms. The paper argues that similar conclusions can reach readers through quite different framings. Users should therefore evaluate an AI's premises and language critically rather than accept its answers passively.

documents.abstract: Biosignals collected from wearable devices are widely utilized in healthcare applications. Machine learning models used in these applications often rely on features extracted from biosignals due to their effectiveness, lower data dimensionality, and wide compatibility across various model architectures. However, existing feature extraction methods often lack task-specific contextual knowledge, struggle to identify optimal features in high-dimensional combinatorial feature space, and are prone to automated code generation and execution errors. In this paper, we propose DeepFeature, the first LLM-empowered, context-aware feature generation framework for wearable biosignals. DeepFeature introduces a multi-source feature generation mechanism that integrates the inherent ability of LLMs, expert knowledge and inter-feature interactions. It also employs an iterative feature refinement process that uses feature assessment-based feedback for feature re-selection. Additionally, DeepFeature utilizes a robust multi-layer filtering and verification approach for feature description-to-code translation to ensure that the feature extraction functions run without crashing. Experimental evaluation results show that DeepFeature achieves the highest average AUROC across eight tasks under both sample-level and subject-level settings, outperforming the best baselines by 4.60% and 4.61%, respectively. DeepFeature achieves the most pronounced gains on the PPG-BP tasks, while remaining competitive with the best-performing baselines on Epilepsy, WESAD, and our self-collected SEN dataset.

The development of edge intelligence has been essential for autonomous drones and vehicular communications due to their ability to provide fast decision-making and real-time analytics. Nonetheless, edge artificial intelligence is highly susceptible to adversarial attacks that affect sensor inputs, resulting in malfunctioning during activities such as navigation, object recognition, To mitigate the risks posed by adversarial attacks, this chapter introduces a novel defense-oriented edge intelligence solution designed to identify and counteract malicious activity in autonomous aerial and vehicular vehicles. Specifically, includes adversarial input detection, robustness through deep learning, mitigation measures, and federated edge learning. Furthermore, XAI is also used to increase accountability in decision-making processes. Through experiments based on LiDAR, radar, and GPS data sets, the defense-aware system significantly enhances attack detection rates, lowers adversarial success rates, and ensures real-time performance without imposing additional computational burdens.

ABSTRACT Background Dental magnification devices provide measurable clinical and ergonomic benefits; however, their adoption among undergraduate dental students remains limited in many institutions. This study aimed to assess awareness, usage patterns, attitudes, perceived barriers, and educational preferences regarding dental magnification among students at the School of Dentistry, University of Jordan. Methods A cross‐sectional questionnaire‐based survey was conducted among 802 dental students at different educational levels, including preclinical third‐year students, clinical undergraduate students in the fourth and fifth years, and postgraduate trainees. Associations between demographic and educational variables and magnification‐related responses were analysed using the chi‐square and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Statistical significance was established at p < 0.05. Results Only 128 students (16.0%) reported clinical use of dental magnification, with significantly higher usage among postgraduate students (34.6%) compared with third‐year students (12.0%) (χ 2 = 17.558, p = 0.002). Male students reported significantly greater magnification use than female students (22.0% vs. 12.6%, p < 0.001). Despite the low rate of clinical use, most respondents (80.4%) agreed that magnification improves clinical accuracy. Cost was identified as the most common barrier to use (78.3%). Attendance at continuing education courses related to magnification was lowest among interns (14.5%). Most participants (84.0%) supported earlier integration of magnification training into the dental curriculum, with third year identified as the preferred stage for introduction. Conclusions A substantial gap exists between students' positive perceptions of dental magnification and its actual clinical use. Financial barriers and limited curricular integration appear to be the main obstacles to adoption. Earlier incorporation of structured magnification training within undergraduate dental education may improve student exposure and uptake.

This study focuses on the design and implementation of an agentic system based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for automated financial advisory services (Robo-Advisors, RA). The relevance of this study lies in the knowledge limitations of large language models (LLMs) in domain-specific areas, such as the financial sector, where factual errors can lead to direct financial losses and regulatory risks. Based on a literature review, the class of tasks for a modern Robo-Advisor platform suitable for RAG-based solutions has been identified. The purpose of this research is to develop a RAG agent architecture for a Robo-Advisor service and verify its functionality on a working prototype. Functional requirements for an RA module were established to track the behaviour of financial assets within a specific investment portfolio. An analysis was conducted on the tools used to implement typical interaction scenarios with a RAG system (data acquisition, text preprocessing, vectorisation, data normalisation, LLM interaction, etc.). A software architecture was designed in which agent functions (obtaining stock prices, analysing financial news, automated reports, user communication) are reflected in separate software modules. The system is divided into an asynchronous indexing circuit and a synchronous user interaction circuit. The agent's memory is implemented as hybrid storage, where a relational database serves as the source of truth, and the vector index is a fully recoverable derivative artifact. A method for re-ranking news search results using a normalised time-of-publication coefficient is proposed. User interaction is implemented as a chatbot for a messenger. Pilot operation confirmed that the system meets the established requirements; identified shortcomings and limitations of the agent are described, along with methods for their resolution. The results of this study can be used to integrate RAG agents into full-scale Robo-Advisor services.

documents.abstract: This exploratory, design-oriented pilot case study examines Erwin, a student-centred AI scaffold designed to augment students’ thinking in an interdisciplinary design innovation module. Unlike answer-giving chatbots, Erwin adopts a supportive-critic stance: it provides stage-aware, dialogic scaffolding that widens idea spaces and supports criteria-based consolidation through nudges and commitments. The analysis drew on 1,999 student and Erwin turns organised into 171 sessions nested within 78 student logs, alongside post-module qualitative feedback. The study combined reflexive thematic analysis with a full-corpus, non-inferential descriptive analysis of selected interaction-process indicators, including initiative balance, futures probes, completed repair sequences, and system boundary or refusal episodes. A purposive sample of six final artefacts provided illustrative triangulation of interaction patterns and student project trajectories. The analysis identified four practices: disciplined divergence, in which Deliberate Cognitive Friction (DCF) prompts appeared alongside expanded frames without displacing agency; criteria-aware convergence, in which students translated broadened views into clearer problem statements, constraints, and next steps; cognitive resilience visible through repair and persistence sequences; and a supportive-critic experience shaped by answer resistance and meta-reflection. As this was a single-course pilot with no control condition, the descriptive indicators characterise observed interaction processes and contextualise the qualitative interpretation; they are not estimates of causal effects or direct measures of learning outcomes. Across cases, these practices appeared alongside traces of broadened ideation, criteria-guided consolidation, and futures-oriented reasoning in the illustrative artefact sample. The paper contributes situated empirical evidence for studying AI as human augmentation rather than substitution; a transferable design blueprint that operationalises DCF at the prompt policy layer through explainable prompts, resilience guardrails, and instrumentation for scaffolding-oriented LLM systems; and a process-oriented operationalisation of cognitive resilience for Human Computer Interaction in education, understood as interactional evidence of repair, persistence, and flexible reframing rather than as a demonstrated learning effect. The discussion offers implications for designing resilient, trust-preserving human-AI ecosystems that balance augmentation against risks of overreliance and cognitive offloading.

The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education is fundamentally transforming pedagogical practices, learning environments, and the roles of teachers and learners. While AI-driven systems offer considerable potential for personalization, efficiency, and data-informed decision-making, their educational value depends on how they are pedagogically framed, critically implemented, and ethically embedded within learning processes. This chapter argues that design thinking provides a robust, human-centered framework for aligning AI innovation with pedagogical goals, learner needs, and ethical considerations. Drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives from educational research, human-centered design, and AI studies, the chapter conceptualizes design thinking as a methodological and pedagogical bridge between technological advancement and meaningful learning design. It demonstrates how key design thinking principles—such as empathy, problem framing, iterative prototyping, and reflective evaluation—can guide the development of AI-enhanced learning environments. Building on this foundation, the chapter introduces a design-driven model for AI integration in education and illustrates its application in practice. It further examines implications for teaching and professional development, emphasizing a shift from tool-centered adoption toward competence-oriented, reflective, and ethically grounded pedagogical design. By positioning design thinking as a strategic framework for the responsible and human-centered integration of AI, the chapter contributes to current debates on rethinking pedagogy in the digital age and offers a structured approach to designing future-oriented learning environments.

documents.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into educational settings requires a fundamental reconsideration of how teachers are prepared for practice. This chapter argues that design thinking, an iterative, human-centered methodology for problem-solving and innovation, offers a particularly productive framework for reshaping teacher education so that graduates are equipped not merely to use AI tools but also to evaluate them critically, adapt them pedagogically, and deploy them ethically. Drawing on scholarship in design thinking, teacher professional learning, AI in education, and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK), the chapter maps the conceptual and practical terrain of AI-ready teacher preparation. It examines the current state of teacher education, identifies persistent gaps in preparing educators for AI-infused classrooms, and proposes an integrated Design Thinking for AI-Ready Teaching (DT-ART) model. The chapter concludes with implications for curriculum designers, teacher educators, and institutional policymakers navigating the digital transformation of schooling.

The explosive rise of short-form videos (SFVs), commonly exemplified by social media reels, has significantly reshaped adolescents’ attention patterns, driven by neurocognitive mechanisms such as novelty seeking, rapid feedback, and dopaminergic reward cycles. While these mechanisms are often associated with distraction, compulsive media use, and reduced sustained attention in teenagers, they also reveal untapped potential for educational design constraining ethically and pedagogically. This chapter proposes a conceptual framework that integrates Design Thinking (DT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to repurpose the engagement affordances of SFVs for the development of sustainable science learning among adolescents. Within the framework, SFVs function as controlled attention-entry triggers that introduce real-world scientific phenomena in brief, engaging formats tailored to adolescent cognitive styles. Design Thinking structures learner engagement into finite, reflective inquiry cycles, supporting agency and problem-solving, two key developmental needs during adolescence. AI operates as an adaptive orchestration layer, supporting personalized pacing, cognitive load regulation, and formative feedback, while intentionally avoiding the addictive dynamics typical of commercial media platforms. By re-engineering short-form engagement within structured pedagogical loops, the framework transforms momentary attention capture into disciplined scientific inquiry, systems-oriented reasoning, and durable conceptual understanding. This chapter contributes to emerging discussions on attention-aware pedagogy for youth, offering a theoretically grounded approach to align digital engagement mechanisms with the long-term sustainability of science learning processes for adolescent learners.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education with intelligent learning systems, automated administration, research support, academic assessment, and institutional decision-making. As Indian Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increasingly incorporate AI-enabled technologies, the lack of a standardized framework for evaluating institutional readiness for responsible AI governance has become a significant policy and administrative challenge. Current evaluation mechanisms primarily emphasize digital infrastructure and technology adoption, neglecting critical aspects such as ethical governance, institutional policy, regulatory compliance, data governance, academic integrity, human capacity development, and transparency, accountability, and risk management. In this paper, we propose developing an AI Governance Readiness Index (AIGRI) as a multidimensional framework to evaluate the preparedness of Indian Higher Education Institutions for the responsible and sustainable adoption of AI. The proposed index is structured around eight interconnected dimensions: Institutional Leadership and Governance, AI Policy and Regulatory Compliance, Digital Infrastructure, Data Governance and Cybersecurity, Human Capacity and AI Literacy, Ethical and Responsible AI Practices, Academic and Research Integrity, and Continuous Evaluation and Innovation. Each dimension is associated with measurable indicators that enable institutions to assess their current status, identify governance gaps, and formulate evidence-based strategies for improvement. The study employs a qualitative doctrinal and policy research approach, underpinned by an extensive review of national education policies, AI governance frameworks, international ethical AI guidelines, and literature on higher education quality assurance. The paper proposes a preliminary scoring model based on principles of responsible AI, good governance, and institutional accountability, which can then be validated through empirical research with universities across India. The proposed AIGRI is a practical governance tool for university administrators, policymakers, accreditation agencies, and regulatory bodies to assess AI readiness systematically. It also contributes to the emerging discourse of AI governance by shifting the focus from technology adoption to institutional preparedness, ethical implementation, and governance maturity. The framework could be a valuable addition to national quality assurance efforts, such as NAAC. It could be aligned with India’s vision of digitally empowered, globally competitive, and socially responsible higher education institutions. The study concludes that the development of a standardized AI Governance Readiness Index can guide policy decisions, enhance institutional resilience, encourage responsible AI adoption, and aid sustainable transformation of higher education in the era of intelligent technologies.

documents.abstract: Fostering sustained interest in physical education among middle school students is regarded as an important factor in improving the effectiveness of school physical education within the framework of the updated educational content in the Republic of Kazakhstan. At the same time, declining student motivation highlights the need for pedagogical approaches that can enhance students’ engagement in the educational process. The purpose of this study was to develop and experimentally evaluate a pedagogical model aimed at fostering middle school students’ interest in physical education. The study was conducted at Kanysh Satpayev Gymnasium in Karaganda, Kazakhstan, and involved students from Grades 6B and 6G. The research methods included a review of the scientific literature, a questionnaire survey, pedagogical observation, physical fitness testing, a pedagogical experiment, and statistical analysis. The proposed pedagogical model was based on the integrated use of game-based, interactive, and digital educational technologies designed to enhance students’ cognitive engagement and personal interest in physical education. The experimental results demonstrated a positive change in students’ level of interest in physical education: the proportion of students with a high level of interest increased from 22.39% to 44.48%, whereas the proportion of students with a low level of interest decreased from 27.22% to 15.16%. In addition, improvements in the physical fitness of students in the experimental group were observed. The findings provide evidence supporting the effectiveness of the proposed pedagogical model and suggest its potential applicability to the organization of physical education in general secondary schools in the Republic of Kazakhstan.

Background Clinical history-taking is a core medical competency, but conventional teaching may be limited by patient availability, variable clinical exposure, and restricted opportunities for repeated practice. Large language models (LLMs) may support simulated practice; however, their clinical, linguistic, and cultural suitability requires careful evaluation in multilingual settings. Objective This study aimed to develop and expert-evaluate a culturally and linguistically adapted English–Malay clinical dialogue corpus and to descriptively benchmark a fine-tuned LLM framework for clinical history-taking simulation in Malaysian undergraduate medical education. Methods A multiphase mixed-methods development and evaluation study was conducted across nine internal medicine systems. Of 63,250 AI-generated dialogue entries, each comprising a simulated doctor inquiry and corresponding patient response, 59,184 (93.6%) underwent consultant-level subject matter expert review using an author-developed holistic 5-point rubric informed by clinical relevance, accuracy, clarity and coherence, completeness, and human-likeness. Free-text comments were analysed inductively. After SME evaluation and clinical-quality and mechanical filtering, 58,886 entries across 2,497 simulated patient profiles were retained. The profiles were partitioned into 1,997 training profiles, 250 validation profiles, and 250 held-out test profiles. Four model configurations were descriptively benchmarked using the same held-out profiles and an automated large language model judge. This benchmark was intended for internal model comparison and did not constitute independent external or human clinical validation of the post-fine-tuning model outputs. Results Mean subject matter expert scores were 4.52/5 for simulated doctor inquiries and 4.58/5 for simulated patient responses. Qualitative analysis identified recurring limitations involving question structure, incomplete probing, repetition, linguistic accuracy, over-explanation, and simulated-patient realism. In descriptive benchmarking, the fine-tuned model achieved the highest observed mean score among the four configurations evaluated. Conclusions Developing a consultant-reviewed, culturally adapted English–Malay clinical dialogue corpus and using it to fine-tune an LLM for simulated history-taking was feasible. The fine-tuned model achieved the highest observed score in the internal automated benchmark, but this finding does not establish statistical, clinical, or educational superiority. The post-fine-tuning model outputs were not independently evaluated by clinicians in the present study. The framework may offer a scalable, contextually relevant supplement to clinical communication training, but blinded human evaluation of post-fine-tuning outputs, targeted safety assessment, external validation, and learner-outcome evaluation are required before routine student-facing implementation.

Rockfall mitigation projects involve high occupational health and safety (OHS) risks due to steep topography, hardto-access work zones, rope-access operations, and environmental uncertainties. In such projects, conventional supervision and communication practices may be limited by blind spots, restricted visibility, and difficult terrain conditions. This study develops and field-evaluates an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based supervision framework to support OHS planning and operational coordination in rope-access operations carried out within rockfall mitigation projects. A descriptive and exploratory field-based research design was adopted. Questionnaire data were collected from 128 Rope Access Technicians (RATs) working in 16 active rockfall mitigation projects in different regions of Türkiye. The survey examined participants’ professional profiles, accident experiences, safety checks, communication and supervision practices, UAV awareness, UAV-related training status, and perceptions regarding UAV-supported monitoring. Field observations were also used to document the physical and operational characteristics of rope-access worksites. Based on the survey findings and field observations, a UAV-based supervision framework was structured around real-time visual monitoring, blind-spot reduction, communication support, hazard observation, and operational coordination. The proposed framework was then examined through a single-site pilot implementation in an active rockfall mitigation project. The findings indicate that RATs generally perceive UAV-supported monitoring and communication as potentially useful for improving situational awareness and supporting field coordination. The pilot implementation provided observational evidence that UAVs can assist supervisors by extending visual access to hardto-observe work areas. However, the study does not claim to demonstrate quantitative reductions in accident rates, work duration, or costs. The proposed UAV-based framework should therefore be considered a complementary decision-support and supervision tool rather than a replacement for trained rope-access supervision.

Motorcycle couriers in the platform-based gig economy are exposed to substantial occupational risks, yet no validated instrument exists to measure their occupational health and safety (OHS) awareness. This study develops and validates the Occupational Safety Awareness Scale for Motorcycle Couriers (OSAS-MC) to address this gap. Drawing on Türkiye’s OHS Law No. 6331, international OHS standards, and feedback from five domain experts, an initial item pool was generated and refined into a 30-item, six-dimensional instrument covering OHS Legislation Knowledge, OHS Practices, Personal Protective Equipment Use, Motorbike Use, OHS Exposure, and OHS Risk Factors. The scale was administered to 265 actively employed motorcycle couriers in Türkiye. Exploratory factor analysis supported a six-factor solution explaining 67.79% of the variance, and confirmatory factor analysis indicated an acceptable model fit (CFI = 0.875; RMSEA = 0.076; χ²/df = 2.543). Internal consistency was high overall (Cronbach’s α = 0.878) and across sub-dimensions (α = 0.805–0.895), and item discrimination was confirmed via upper-lower 27% group comparisons. The OSAS-MC offers a reliable, context-sensitive instrument for assessing safety awareness in high-risk, platform-mediated delivery work, and provides policymakers, platform operators, and labour organisations with a diagnostic tool to identify awareness gaps and guide targeted interventions.

Abstract Developments in the field of photography and the contribution of artificial intelligence have been remarkable in a developing India. The journey from early optical and chemical processes to digital visual communication has been significant. Technologies ranging from everyday applications to film, digital photography, smart photography, cloud platforms, machine learning, generative AI, drones, and IoT devices (such as Alexa) have vastly expanded the possibilities for capturing, processing, interpreting, and sharing images. Modern photography is no longer limited to just cameras, lenses, digital sensors, and photographers; smart technologies are increasingly playing a pivotal role in processes such as focusing, exposure, color correction, noise reduction, dynamic range enhancement, subject recognition, image segmentation, autofocus, image enhancement, and post-production. Research into AI and photography indicates that machine learning and computational processing have transformed the traditional boundaries between image capture and image processing. In India, these changes are unfolding within a digital framework. The Government of India’s 'IndiaAI' mission received approval in March 2024, aiming to strengthen computing infrastructure, data availability, AI innovation, and world-class development. This emerging technology ecosystem directly impacts photography and visual media education, as well as professional fields such as journalism, advertising, fashion product imaging, scientific documentation, wildlife and heritage conservation, and the creative industries. Furthermore, generative AI is driving a profound transformation; images can now be enhanced, recreated, modified, or generated from scratch without every visible element being directly linked to an optical phenomenon. This opens up new creative opportunities. However, issues regarding authenticity, the author's copyright, privacy, consent, employment, cultural representation, and public trust also arise. This research paper examines the historical evolution of photography, the opportunities for India in the field of photography alongside smart technology, the challenges faced by photographers and educators, and a proposed framework for responsible photography in a developing India.

OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) systems for detecting proximal caries lesions on bitewing radiographs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Electronic searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based systems for proximal caries detection on bitewing radiographs were included. True-positive, false-positive, true-negative, and false-negative values were extracted directly or reconstructed from reported diagnostic accuracy metrics when sufficient information was available. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated separately using random-effects models on the logit scale. RESULTS: Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which three studies provided sufficient 2×2 contingency table data for quantitative synthesis. The pooled sensitivity and specificity of AI systems for proximal caries detection were 0.73 (95% CI 0.70–0.75) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.69–0.99), respectively. Most included studies demonstrated promising diagnostic performance using deep learning architectures, particularly convolutional neural networks and YOLO-based models. CONCLUSION: AI systems demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for detecting proximal caries lesions on bitewing radiographs. However, methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation remain important limitations. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm the clinical applicability of AI-assisted caries detection systems.

The objective of this research is to identify, characterize, and analyze artificial intelligence (AI) applications used in the Mexican public sector. A quantitative methodology using descriptive statistics was used. The analysis shows that the use of AI in the Mexican public sector is concentrated in the Executive Branch and in sectors related to security, justice, government, economy, finance, and transparency. This technology is primarily used to improve communication with citizens and to increase organizational efficiency, employing natural language processing and machine learning to perform interaction tasks through chatbots and in image, voice, and text recognition tasks. The use of AI in the Mexican public sector presents marked institutional, territorial, sectoral, and functional asymmetries. It also reflects a strong technological dependence on the private sector and the need to strengthen internal capacities.

AI systems that research a topic rely on what is published on the web. Much useful knowledge is not published. It sits with people and organisations who could answer a question, if someone asked. dialogue.txt is a small, machine-readable file on a website (/.well-known/dialogue.txt). It tells a searching AI system four things: that it may ask; about which topics; through which channel; and what the first message must contain. The first message only proposes a bridge. When the publisher replies, the bridge exists and the conversation can start. The file permits talk, never action. An example. An AI system researches traffic flow. A navigation company's dialogue.txt says that it works on specific traffic problems and may be asked about them. Without the file, the system can at best report that the company exists. If the solution is not public, it is missed. With the file, the system can ask. This record contains the specification, the field registry, a fill-in template, examples, a validator, a local try-it page, the test summary (five language models from five providers, more than 3,500 recorded model calls) and the Internet-Draft draft-wolf-dialogue-txt-00. About the author. Dimitri Wolf is an engineer. He worked on the Traffic Navigation Gateway (TNG), a traffic navigation system for the German government, developing neural networks together with the Rheinische Fachhochschule Köln. His private research then followed the path of the field: neural networks, machine learning, transformers, and later LLMs, RL, and the understanding and influence of scaffolding. dialogue.txt is a private research project, not his job and not a product. The ideas behind it grew over about ten years of this research. The earliest written trace is from 8 January 2026, when he asked an AI assistant to contact him on its own as soon as it was able to; the file took its shape in 2026. documents.abstract: This study examines the extent to which family values vary according to socio-demographic determinants -gender, age, educational attainment, occupational status, and mode of spouse acquaintance. Data were collected from 287 parents of primary school- age children in Düzce, Turkey, using the Family Values Scale, and analyzed through independent-samples t tests and one-way ANOVA. The findings indicate that women attach greater significance to the mother–child relationship and participatory decision-making, whereas men emphasize kinship ties, childrearing, marriage, spousal loyalty, and the economic functions of the family, reflecting more traditional orientations. Self-initiated marriages were associated with stronger emotional bonds. Younger respondents expressed more liberal attitudes toward sexuality and unconventional values, middle-aged participants prioritized democratic decision-making, and older participants showed stronger adherence to marital commitment and loyalty. Education was a critical factor: lower schooling levels corresponded to greater endorsement of traditional norms, and higher levels to more egalitarian orientations. Occupationally, health professionals held more liberal perspectives, while housewives and private-sector employees showed stronger traditional attachments. Overall, family values in Turkey appear shaped simultaneously by socio-demographic characteristics and the interplay between tradition and modernity, underscoring the relevance of policies promoting education, gender equality, and labor force participation

This study aimed to determine the digital competence levels of preservice primary school teachers, examine whether their competence differed according to personal and experiential variables, and investigate the relationship between self-assessed artificial intelligence (AI) use competence and digital competence. The study employed descriptive and correlational survey designs with 119 preservice teachers enrolled in primary school teacher education programs at five universities. Data were collected through a Personal Information Form, which included a single-item self-assessment of AI use competence, and the 25-item, five-dimensional Teacher Digital Competence Scale. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression were used. Overall digital competence was high. Scores did not differ significantly by gender, age, year of study, previous digital technology training, or previous AI training. Participants with digital material development experience had significantly higher competence (Hedges’ g = 0.76). Self-assessed AI use competence was strongly and positively associated with overall digital competence (r = .646) and accounted for 41.7% of its variance. The findings suggest that active digital production and AI-supported material development experiences are associated with stronger digital competence and deserve attention in teacher education.

This study investigates how digital entrepreneurship drives high performance in Jordanian financial services companies and clarifies the human and organizational learning mechanisms behind this link. Survey data from 221 managers across 27 firms (proportional stratified sampling) measured five dimensions of digital entrepreneurship (digital leadership, knowledge, finance, culture, innovation) and four dimensions of high performance (continuous improvement, workforce quality, teamwork, flexible work systems). Descriptive statistics (SPSS) and PLS-SEM revealed a significant positive effect of digital entrepreneurship on high performance, with digital leadership, digital culture, and digital innovation emerging as the strongest predictors. Findings position digital transformation as a capability-building process: firms that institutionalize continuous digital upskilling, codify knowledge-sharing routines, align leadership and culture with innovation governance, and invest in FinTech-enabled processes and data capabilities achieve more robust high-performance work systems. The study contributes applied insights for educational studies and the applied humanities by framing digital entrepreneurship as a learning organization endeavor—where human-centered change, workforce development, and collaborative practices translate technology adoption into sustained performance. Practically, managers should embed structured learning pathways, cross-functional teamwork, and flexible work design to accelerate improvement. Sector-specific evidence from an emerging economy extends the literature and offers actionable guidance for policy and practice in digitally evolving financial services.

The rapid expansion of digital technologies has fundamentally transformed how education is delivered, accessed, and experienced across the globe. This paper examines the relationship between digital learning and social inclusion, exploring whether technology-mediated education advances or undermines equity in the twenty-first century. Drawing on a review of literature published between 2019 and 2026, the study investigates how digital tools, ranging from remote learning platforms to artificial intelligence-driven personalization systems, shape access to quality education for historically marginalized groups, including low-income students, learners with disabilities, rural populations, and linguistic minorities. The paper adopts a qualitative, desk-based research methodology, synthesizing peer-reviewed studies, international policy reports, and systematic reviews to map the enabling conditions and persistent barriers associated with digital educational equity. Findings indicate that while digital learning holds considerable potential to widen access, personalize instruction, and support diverse learners through assistive and adaptive technologies, this potential is unevenly realized due to persistent digital divides in infrastructure, device access, connectivity, and digital literacy. The analysis further reveals that artificial intelligence-enabled tools can both mitigate and exacerbate educational inequality depending on how thoughtfully they are designed, governed, and deployed. The paper concludes that achieving genuine educational equity in a digitally mediated era requires deliberate policy intervention, inclusive design principles, and sustained investment in infrastructure and teacher capacity, rather than reliance on technology diffusion alone. Recommendations include embedding equity audits into EdTech procurement, strengthening digital literacy programs for underserved communities, and prioritizing universal design for learning within national digital education strategies.

Abstract: Scientific literature has shown an association between the use of digital technologies and the mental health of higher education students. However, gaps remain regarding the digital practices used to promote mental health literacy. In this context, a qualitative study was conducted using six focus groups, involving 43 students from 32 courses at 18 Portuguese higher education institutions. Thematic analysis of the data identified five themes: Digital habits; Digital technologies in mentalhealth literacy; Impact of digital technologies on well-being and mental health; Evaluation of digital technologies in mental health; Good practices in promoting well-being and mental health. The results show that the focus groups provided spaces for critical reflection and collective construction of knowledge concerning the benefits, risks and limitations of digital technologies in mental health. However, a discrepancy was identified between the participants’ critical discourse and their actualpractices. Despite reservations about the use of non-specialist digital tools, there is widespread reliance on social media content and artificial intelligence. This finding highlights a focus on immediacy, anonymity and accessibility, underscoring the need to gain a better understanding of these mechanisms and to improve access to specialist services.

The digital transformation of education has significantly changed approaches to teaching and learning in higher education. Traditional teacher-centered instruction is increasingly being supplemented by interactive, personalized, and student-centered learning models supported by digital technologies. This article examines the pedagogical potential of learning management systems, digital communication platforms, artificial intelligence tools, multimedia resources, virtual learning environments, and online assessment technologies. The study employs theoretical analysis and synthesis of contemporary educational research. The results suggest that digital technologies can strengthen students’ autonomy, collaboration, critical thinking, motivation, and access to educational resources when they are integrated according to clearly defined pedagogical objectives. At the same time, excessive dependence on technology, digital inequality, academic integrity problems, information overload, and insufficient digital competence among educators remain important challenges. The paper argues that the effectiveness of educational digitalization depends not on the quantity of technological tools but on their pedagogically appropriate application. Keywords: digital education, student-centered learning, higher education, educational technology, digital competence, active learning, pedagogy

This study examines the implementation process and operational conditions determining the success or failure of the digital transformation of disaster response in Wajima City, Ishikawa Prefecture, following the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake. The study is based on a single-case comparative analysis of five operations—post-earthquake building safety assessment, shelter management, temporary housing, facility management, and publicly funded demolition—using operational records, products, meeting materials, and development logs. These operations were compared using five dimensions: digitalization of information collection, accumulation of shareable data, situational awareness through visualization, connection to decision support, and cross-departmental coordination. Among the five operations, post-earthquake building safety assessment and temporary housing advanced most continuously, while shelter management and facility management tended to remain at the stage of visualization, and publicly funded demolition remained fragmented. The results reveal that the digital transformation of disaster response progressed step by step from data input to accumulation, visualization, and decision support, rather than emerging all at once. Self-contained operations tended to advance more smoothly, whereas cross-departmental operations required clearer coordination and decision-making mechanisms. Thus, success depended less on technology itself than on operational conditions, implying that effective implementation depends on the peacetime preparation of data items, identifiers, update responsibilities, and decision-making arrangements.

Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 seeks to transform the country into a developed nation by the centenary of independence. Municipal corporations have a central role in this transformation because the quality of urban governance directly affects citizens’ everyday lives, economic activity, environmental sustainability and social well-being. Rapid urbanisation, increasing demand for public services, climate-related risks and growing expectations for transparent administration have created a need for municipal institutions to adopt digital technologies. This paper examines the opportunities and challenges associated with the digital transformation of municipal corporations in India. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, geographic information systems, cloud computing, digital payment systems, data analytics, Internet of Things applications and online citizen-service platforms can improve municipal administration. Particular attention is given to digital revenue collection, solid-waste management, water and sanitation services, urban planning, grievance redressal, traffic management and citizen participation. The paper argues that digital transformation should not be understood merely as the computerisation of existing municipal processes. Instead, it should involve institutional reform, data-driven decision-making, inclusive service delivery, employee capacity building, cybersecurity and sustainable urban development. At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

At the same time, municipalities face challenges including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, shortage of skilled personnel, fragmented databases, cybersecurity risks, unequal access to technology and resistance to organisational change. The paper proposes a citizen-centric and sustainable digital governance framework through which municipal corporations can contribute meaningfully to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

Abstract India's vision of Vikshit Bharat @2047 rests on building a digitally empowered, innovation-driven, and sustainable economy in which artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure serve as engines of inclusive growth. Realising this vision depends critically on the quality of human capital that education systems produce, and teacher education stands at the centre of that pipeline. This paper examines how the digital transformation envisaged under Vikshit Bharat @2047 is reshaping teacher education in India, using the reforms introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 as the entry point. It discusses how national digital platforms such as DIKSHA, SWAYAM, and PM eVIDYA, together with emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, blockchain, and the Internet of Things, are creating new possibilities for personalised, inclusive, and lifelong teacher development. The paper also situates these developments within the wider digital economy, arguing that a technologically competent teaching workforce is a precondition for the commerce, innovation, and productivity gains that Vikshit Bharat @2047 anticipates. At the same time, the paper identifies significant risks, including the digital divide, uneven digital literacy among teachers, and adverse effects of excessive technology use on mental well-being, sleep, and attention. Drawing on secondary literature and policy documents, the paper proposes a blended and sustainability-oriented framework for teacher education that combines digital tools with face-to-face mentoring, structured digital wellness training, and continuous monitoring of technology use. It concludes that India's digital future will be strongest where digital ambition is matched with digital responsibility, and where teacher education is treated as strategic national infrastructure rather than a peripheral concern.

Digital Twin technology has emerged as a transformative approach in modern healthcare by enabling the creation of patient-specific virtual replicas that accurately represent anatomical structures and physiological behavior. This paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence based Digital Twin framework for surgical rehearsal and preoperative planning that integrates medical imaging, three-dimensional reconstruction, and predictive AI models to assist surgeons in evaluating surgical strategies before entering the operating room. The proposed framework utilizes Computed Tomography and Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans to generate a personalized three-dimensional digital model of the patient's organ. Artificial Intelligence techniques are employed for image segmentation, anatomical structure identification, risk prediction, and simulation analysis. Surgeons can interact with the virtual model to perform multiple rehearsal scenarios, evaluate different surgical approaches, and estimate possible complications before the actual procedure. The framework aims to reduce surgical uncertainty, improve procedural accuracy, minimize intraoperative risks, and support informed clinical decision making. In addition, the proposed system offers educational benefits by providing a realistic training environment for medical students and surgical residents without exposing patients to unnecessary risks. The architecture is designed to be scalable and can be extended to multiple medical specialties, including cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedic surgery, and organ transplantation. By combining Artificial Intelligence with Digital Twin technology, the proposed framework demonstrates significant potential to enhance surgical precision, improve patient safety, optimize healthcare resources, and advance the future of personalized medicine.

documents.abstract: AI agents are moving from systems that only generate information to systems that can plan tasks, use tools, and perform operations through external APIs. This shift creates a security problem that traditional permission models do not fully address: an agent may hold broad privileges even when a particular task needs only a small part of that access. A valid token therefore does not automatically mean that every action produced by the agent is appropriate. This paper proposes DPMF (Dynamic Risk-Aware Permission Framework), an external authorization layer for AI agents that interact with third-party services. DPMF evaluates each proposed API action using contextual signals such as user-intent alignment, data sensitivity, permission severity, source trust, action reversibility, and behavioral deviation. The resulting risk level drives one of four decisions: Allow, Restrict, Human Approval, or Deny. The framework also separates the agent's ability to propose an action from the security layer's authority to approve it. The paper presents the framework architecture, threat model, risk-scoring approach, dynamic permission algorithm, case study, and an experimental methodology for comparing DPMF with static authorization. Because the framework has not yet been experimentally implemented, no numerical performance claims are presented as established results. Instead, measurable evaluation criteria and expected outcomes are defined.

With the widespread adoption of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS), the need for effective ADAS driver training increases. However, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of ADAS education remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of an ADAS driver training program across four European countries. The training included classroom-based theoretical instruction and practical hands-on experience on test-tracks and open-roads. 166 participants completed a questionnaire measuring their knowledge, attitudes, and behavioral intentions towards ADAS pre- and post-training. Overall knowledge of system purpose, handling and limitations improved significantly with the training. However, some misunderstandings remained, and in some cases, misconceptions from before the training were not corrected. Perceived safety and trust remained unchanged while willingness to use ADAS systems, and the perceived ease of use and usefulness of ADAS increased. Future training should not only provide information for trainees but also identify misconceptions they may hold. Follow-up or feedback sessions are recommended to address potential misunderstandings.

documents.abstract: Chronic or recurrent pain significantly impairs quality of life, and conventional pharmacological treatments often produce side effects, motivating the search for non-pharmacological alternatives. This study introduces a novel paradigm — E-Tactile Tactile Flow (E-Tactile Flow)—which integrates electrotactile stimulation with attentional engagement and flow-related task design. Inspired by a bidirectional attention mechanism, the paradigm designed goal-directed task mode and stimulus-driven task mode to examine the role of cognitive engagement in pain modulation. A preliminary study validated the feasibility and safety parameters of an 8×8 electrotactile system. In Experiment 1 (n = 42), both attention modes effectively reduced pain perception, with the goal-directed task mode showing significantly stronger modulation of several physiological measures and a marginal trend toward lower subjective pain ratings than the stimulus-driven task mode. Building on this, Experiment 2 introduced adaptive difficulty modulation to better align task challenge with participant performance. Results showed that dynamic task adjustment significantly enhanced attentional engagement and reduced pain ratings. Overall, this study provides initial empirical support for an electrotactile interaction paradigm for non-pharmacological pain modulation.

EcoPro-LSTM is version 0 of Ecosystem Process Modelling using a Long Short-Term Memory Approach. The model uses a Multi-Task Multi-Timescale Long Short-Term Memory (MT-LSTM) modelling framework. EcoPro-LSTM was developed by Mitra Cattry et al. as part of the research “EcoPro-LSTM v0: A Memory-based Machine Learning Approach to Predicting Ecosystem Dynamics across Time Scales in Mediterranean Environments,” accepted for publication in Machine Learning: Earth (2026). The work was financially supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation, Award #P500PN_206603, and the National Science Foundation (NSF) Science and Technology Center (STC) Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP), Award #2019625-STC. The model predicts environmental variables including gross primary productivity (carbon uptake), ecosystem respiration, evapotranspiration, and surface soil moisture across multiple timescales using a single LSTM architecture, as described in the accompanying tutorial. Integrated gradients are used to enhance model interpretability by identifying the influence of climatic drivers such as precipitation. For questions, issues, or further assistance with the code, please contact Mitra Cattry at mitra.cattry@gmail.com. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence edge computing, and autonomous systems is transforming the nature of modern warfare. Traditional defense operations, which relied heavily on centralized command structures and human decision-making, are increasingly being augmented by intelligent systems capable of sensing, analyzing, and responding to dynamic battlefield conditions in real time. Among these technologies, Edge AI has emerged as a critical enabler of smart warfare by allowing data processing and AI inference to occur directly on deployed platforms rather than relying on distant cloud infrastructures. This chapter explores the role of Edge AI in defense operations, with particular emphasis on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), autonomous surveillance systems and intelligent reconnaissance platforms. It further examines the use of Edge AI for applications such as target recognition, battlefield situational awareness, autonomous navigation, mission execution, and decentralized decision-making.

Introduction This study examines the pedagogical integration of educommunication and artificial intelligence (AI) and its association with self-reported professional competencies among university prosumers-students who simultaneously consume, produce, and share academic content through digital platforms. Methods A non-experimental, cross-sectional quantitative design with descriptive-correlational and structural purposes was employed. Data were collected using a psychometrically validated 26-item Likert-scale questionnaire (plus six open-response items) administered to a convenience sample of 547 university students enrolled at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Ecuador. The instrument assessed five dimensions: (1) AI-mediated learning processes, (2) educommunication and expression, (3) knowledge prosumption, (4) perceived professional competencies, and (5) ethics and critical AI use. Psychometric validation confirmed excellent reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.91; McDonald's ω = 0.93). Exploratory factor analysis supported the five-factor structure (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.91; Bartlett's test p < 0.001; variance explained = 61.4%). Confirmatory factor analysis indicated a satisfactory model fit (comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.96; Tucker-Lewis index [TLI] = 0.95; root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.052; standardized root mean square residual [SRMR] = 0.061). A single-factor test yielded a first unrotated factor accounting for 28.3% of the variance, below the 50% threshold, offering a preliminary indication against a single dominant method factor, although this test alone does not rule out common method bias (see Section 3.3). Results Structural equation modeling revealed significant direct paths from AI-mediated learning to perceived professional competencies ( β = 0.58, p < 0.001) and from educommunication to knowledge prosumption ( β = 0.51, p < 0.001), with knowledge prosumption partially mediating the educommunication-competency association ( β _indirect = 0.21; R² = 0.74 for D3; R² = 0.78 for D4), and ethics and critical AI use functioning as a significant moderator of the AI learning-competency path (interaction β = 0.34, p < 0.001). Given the cross-sectional, self-report design, these results are interpreted as structural associations rather than causal effects. Discussion Findings indicate that AI integration within educommunicative frameworks is positively associated with autonomous learning, creativity, and digital communication skills. However, risks associated with technological over-reliance and epistemic dependency were also identified in the qualitative data. These findings constitute structurally validated evidence that pedagogical AI integration, framed within educommunicative approaches, is associated with the perceived development of critical, collaborative, and innovative professional competencies in higher education.

Abstract This study examines the effectiveness of structured AI-supported learning in English vocabulary acquisition among undergraduate learners. A quasi-experimental design involved two intact B.A. Part-I student divisions at Shri Vijaysinha Yadav College, Peth Vadgaon. Both groups received instruction covering 100 target vocabulary items in four areas. The Experimental Group received teacher-guided support through an AI-Supported Vocabulary Learning Cycle using NotebookLM and ChatGPT for learning, practice, feedback, and revision. Both groups subsequently completed the same 100 item vocabulary post-test. Independent samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Cohen’s d were used. The Experimental Group achieved a significantly higher overall mean score (75.53) than the Control Group (66.95), t(70) = 6.39, p < .001, d = 1.51. All four categories showed significant differences, strongest for phrasal verbs. Gender showed no significant difference, whereas previous AI exposure and regular smartphone use were associated with higher achievement among Experimental Group learners. The findings suggest that AI can contribute to vocabulary learning when carefully and purposefully integrated with teacher-led classroom instruction and curriculum objectives. AI extends practice, feedback, revision, and application. Overall findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the intact-group design and absence of delayed assessment.
