documents.abstract: This article analyses the effectiveness and perception of occupational safety and health (OSH) training using virtual reality (VR) compared to traditional methods. The aim of the study was to verify the effectiveness of VR training compared to traditional methods (Research No. 1) and to analyse the impressions of participants with different experiences with VR in the training system (Research No. 2). Research No. 1, conducted on students in the fields of construction and occupational health and safety, compared test results after traditional training (in person / online training) and VR (the “VR training at work at height” application). Research No. 2 included active construction workers, analysing their opinions on the usefulness, engagement, and impact of VR training on hazard knowledge, using questionnaires and participant observation. Research No. 1’s results showed a significant improvement in test scores after VRtraining (an average increase of 22%), suggesting a higher effectiveness of this method. In Research No. 2, participants rated highly the usefulness of VR in health and safety training, comfort with VR devices, and their own participation. The results of the study confirm the effectiveness of VR training in occupational safety and health, increasing the effectiveness and participation of participants. Immersion, visualisation, and simulation of harsh working conditions are key advantages of this technology. The VR training system combines the experience of virtual reality with learning theory, simulating emergency response procedures and procedures for the use of personal protective equipment.

Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of a large language model (LLM)-based intelligent adaptive teaching program in improving adverse event risk perception among newly employed nurses. Methods A prospective quasi-experimental study was conducted among 134 newly employed nurses recruited between July 2023 and July 2025 from a campus of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Zhejiang Province, China. Participants received training using an LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program. The Nurses' Risk Perception of Adverse Events Scale (NRPAES), the incidence of nursing adverse events, and training satisfaction were assessed before the intervention and 3 months after training. Differences in these outcomes before and after the intervention were analyzed. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 26.0, with the chi-square test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test used as appropriate. Results Following the LLM-based intelligent adaptive training, the adverse event risk perception score among newly employed nurses increased significantly from 14.95 (11.60, 17.29) before training to 16.22 (12.76, 19.00) after training ( Z = −3.527, P < 0.001). The overall incidence of nursing adverse events decreased significantly from 36 events (1.01‰) before training to 28 events (0.58‰) after training ( χ 2 = 5.060, P = 0.024). Visualization using a Sankey diagram further demonstrated an overall reduction in adverse events after the intervention. In addition, more than 90% of newly employed nurses reported satisfaction with each item of the satisfaction questionnaire for the LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program. Conclusion The LLM-based intelligent adaptive teaching program provides practical support for the individualized delivery of clinical risk perception training for newly employed nurses. The program may improve nurses' ability to perceive adverse event risks. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the integration of LLM-based tools into the design and delivery of nursing education programs.

Job satisfaction is widely recognised as a critical determinant of employee performance, organisational productivity, and long-term institutional effectiveness across diverse economic sectors. This paper examines the relationship between job satisfaction and employee performance through a comparative lens that considers both developed and developing country contexts. Drawing on a systematic literature review of empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025, the study synthesises evidence from a broad range of industries, including education, telecommunications, banking and financial services, information technology, automotive, healthcare, retail, construction, agriculture, logistics, energy, public administration, and manufacturing.The findings reveal a consistently positive and statistically significant association between job satisfaction and employee performance, either directly or through mediating mechanisms such as work engagement, organisational commitment, and motivation. Across sectors, job satisfaction is shaped by a combination of structural and motivational factors, including working conditions, training and development, leadership quality, compensation, career advancement opportunities, organisational support, and job design. Employees who report higher satisfaction levels tend to demonstrate stronger commitment, greater discretionary effort, higher productivity, and improved service quality.

El nuevo Código Ético y Deontológico de la Enfermera Española surge en un momento clave para la profesión, al actualizar un marco que llevaba más de tres décadas sin revisar, al afrontar desafíos en la práctica, investigación y el uso de nuevas tecnologías. El código reconoce la madurez científica alcanzada por la enfermería y establece la investigación como un deber ético esencial para avanzar en nuestra disciplina y mejorar la calidad del cuidado. También incorpora competencias digitales e inteligencia artificial, recordando nuestra responsabilidad profesional en su aplicación. Este Código actualiza valores, amplía compromisos y ofrece un marco ético sólido para una enfermería que reconoce en la investigación el camino para mejorar la calidad de los cuidados y reforzar su impacto en la sociedad. ABSTRACT The new Code of Ethics and Deontology of the Spanish Nurse emerges at a pivotal moment for the profession, updating a framework that had remained unrevised for more than three decades while addressing contemporary challenges in practice, research, and the use of new technologies. The Code acknowledges the scientific maturity attained by nursing and establishes research as an essential ethical duty to advance the discipline and improve the quality of care. It also incorporates digital competencies and artificial intelligence, underscoring our professional responsibility in their implementation. This Code updates core values, expands professional commitments, and provides a robust ethical framework for a nursing discipline that recognizes research as the cornerstone for enhancing quality of care and strengthening its societal impact.

Capturing meaningful everyday moments is challenging as they often occur when users are cognitively absorbed or physically occupied. While always-on recording reduces “misses,” it introduces severe privacy concerns and data triage fatigue. We present EmbodiedRecall, a ring-to-glasses system that operationalizes a proactive capture paradigm. By continuously analyzing fine-grained hand dynamics via dual IMU-equipped rings, the system recognizes compositional motion primitives and utilizes a multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) to infer capture intent within hand-anchorable embodied moments. To balance agency with automation, EmbodiedRecall delivers subtle haptic or visual prompts, allowing users to “confirm-to-commit” short video clips from a privacy-preserving rolling buffer. A controlled lab study ( N = 20) validated our multi-stage pipeline, showing that our model significantly outperforms deep learning baselines with 75.35% accuracy. A 6-day active-session deployment ( N = 13) demonstrated that the system correctly aligns with user intent (46.5% confirmation rate) while surfacing serendipitous, emotionally resonant “micro-moments” users would not have captured manually. We discuss design implications for predictive wearables that enhance socio-emotional preservation while maintaining user agency.

Building fires and industrial thermal disasters rank among the most devastating hazards confronting modern societies, causing thousands of fatalities, billions of dollars in economic losses, and lasting environmental damage each year. The increasing complexity of built environments—including high-rise structures, underground facilities, and chemical processing plants—demands a commensurate advancement in emergency rescue technologies. This review provides a comprehensive examination of state-of-the-art technologies employed in the detection, suppression, and rescue operations associated with building fires and industrial thermal disasters. Key domains covered include early fire detection systems integrating the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning; advanced fire suppression technologies such as water mist, gaseous agents, and high-expansion foam; autonomous and semi-autonomous rescue robotics; unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with thermal imaging; Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital twins for emergency planning and evacuation simulation; personal protective equipment (PPE) advancements including biometric wearables; and communication and situational-awareness systems. Special attention is given to industrial thermal hazards, including petrochemical fires, hazardous material incidents, BLEVE events, and dust explosions. The paper concludes with a critical synthesis of current research gaps and recommendations for future work, emphasizing integrated, data-driven, and human-centered approaches to emergency rescue.

Educational Robots are programmable robotic systems designed or adapted for teaching, learning, training, experimentation, and educational interaction. They can provide learners with opportunities to explore concepts through physical interaction, programming, problem-solving, experimentation, and project-based activities. Robotics brings together multiple areas of knowledge, including Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Electronics, and Design. In education, robots can therefore function not only as technological tools but also as platforms through which students develop computational thinking, creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. Educational robots may range from simple programmable devices used by young learners to sophisticated humanoid or autonomous robots used in higher education and research. Their educational role depends on the learner's age, curriculum, learning objectives, available infrastructure, and level of technological complexity. An Educational Robot is a robotic system used for educational purposes to support teaching, learning, experimentation, or skill development.A simplified learning process is: Learning Objective → Robot Activity → Student Interaction → Experimentation → Feedback → Learning The robot becomes a medium through which students can explore concepts and develop practical skills. The major objectives include: Making learning interactive Developing problem-solving skills Encouraging computational thinking Supporting programming education Promoting STEM learning Encouraging creativity Developing collaboration skills Connecting theory with practical experience Increasing learner engagement The objective is not simply to introduce robots into classrooms but to use robotics meaningfully to achieve educational outcomes. Robotics combines physical hardware with software and programming. A basic robotic learning system can be represented as: Input → Processing → Decision → Action → Feedback For example: Sensor Input → Program Logic → Motor Control → Robot Movement → Environmental Feedback Students can observe how computational instructions produce physical outcomes.

Emotion classification in music is a central problem in affective computing with critical applications in music therapy, personalized media, and emotionally adaptive systems. This study proposes a novel multi-modal stacking ensemble framework for multi-label music emotion recognition using the Emotify dataset. The proposed architecture integrates acoustic features, listener metadata (age, gender, mood), and genre information to capture both perceptual and contextual determinants of emotional response. Six modeling phases were evaluated using Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), XGBoost, and ensemble learning strategies. The final Stacking Ensemble, combining Random Forest, MLP, and XGBoost through a logistic regression meta-classifier, achieved a subset accuracy of 0.41, Hamming loss of 0.25, and macro-averaged F1 score of 0.67, outperforming all individual models as well as recent state-of-the-art approaches evaluated on the same Emotify dataset. Compared with existing CNN-LSTM and LLM-based methods, which report macro-F1 values below 0.51 or rely on shortsegment evaluation, the proposed framework delivers substantially higher performance on full-length music clips with strict multi-label evaluation. The results demonstrate that stacked ensemble learning combined with multi-modal feature fusion provides a robust and generalizable solution for modeling complex emotional landscapes in music, enabling accurate emotionaware music therapy systems, adaptive media platforms, and personalized music recommendation engines.

Abstract India’s digital transformation is creating a growing need for intelligent systems that can operate reliably across diverse sectors and linguistic settings. This paper presents a conceptual review of the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI), mathematics, and India’s digital development. The discussion focuses on agriculture, education, banking and financial services, legal services, transportation, digital commerce, and industry. Particular attention is given to the mathematical ideas that underpin AI: linear algebra for representing data and parameters; probability and statistics for uncertainty and inference; calculus for gradient-based learning; and optimization for selecting model parameters and making decisions. Mathematical modelling is further considered as a bridge between real-world systems and data-driven methods. The paper also examines responsible and inclusive AI, emphasizing reliability, privacy, fairness, transparency, security, accountability, and human oversight. India’s national AI strategy and the India’s AI Mission provide a policy context for these developments, while recent international assessment work highlights the importance of human-centred and ethical deployment. The paper argues that India’s long-term AI capacity should be developed through a coordinated emphasis on computing infrastructure, high-quality data, mathematical education, interdisciplinary research, multilingual technologies, and responsible governance.

This study investigated English-major students’ perceptions of AI-assisted tools in IELTS Writing Task 2 practice at Thanh Do University, Vietnam. The study aimed to explore how students perceived the usefulness and challenges of using AI-assisted writing technologies during IELTS-oriented writing activities. A qualitative research design was employed, involving semi-structured interviews with 15 third-year English-major students enrolled in the Integrated English 2 course during the second semester of the 2025 academic year. The participants had experience using AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, and Gemini to support IELTS Writing Task 2 practice. Interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that students generally perceived AI-assisted writing tools positively due to their usefulness in idea generation, essay organization, grammar correction, vocabulary enhancement, and self-study support. Participants also believed that AI technologies improved writing confidence and encouraged learner autonomy. However, concerns regarding overreliance on AI-generated content, reduced independent thinking, and the reliability of AI-generated feedback were also identified. The study highlights the potential of AI-assisted writing technologies as supplementary learning resources in IELTS-oriented writing instruction while emphasizing the importance of responsible and balanced AI integration in higher education contexts.

documents.abstract: Pronunciation is one of the most difficult areas of second language acquisition and more especially for EFL learners. Typical classroom settings can be difficult to provide individual pronunciation feedback and corrective feedback. The recent developments of Artificial Intelligence (AI) especially language learning through AI speech recognition have revolutionized the way language is learned, providing instant, personalized and data-driven pronunciation feedback. This paper proposes to examine how well AI speech recognition technology can improve the pronunciation skills of learners. The study is based on previous research, theories on second language acquisition, and current advances in education technology to explore the role of AI applications in facilitating pronunciation accuracy, learner autonomy, motivation, and confidence. The paper proposes that in the field of pronunciation learning, continuously assessing and providing immediate corrective feedback on students' pronunciation through AI-based speech recognition technology can generate adaptive learning experiences and effectively enhance pronunciation learning outcomes. However, the potential for educating with them is only realized if a number of issues are tackled, including technology, accent bias, privacy and accessibility. The results indicate that the use of AI pronunciation tools in language teaching could enhance the learning atmosphere and be effective when combined with a classical language teaching method.

This conference paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-based learning environments can enhance student engagement in higher education. The study focuses on the integration of learning analytics, recommendation systems, intelligent tutoring, adaptive feedback, and interactive programming tasks to support behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social engagement. The proposed model links learner profiling, real-time analytics, personalization, feedback, and pedagogical design into a unified engagement-oriented learning environment. A model-based experimental framework is presented with sample indicators and illustrative results. The findings suggest that AI-supported adaptive learning environments may increase student participation, improve persistence in programming tasks, strengthen self-regulated learning, and support the development of programming competence. The paper also discusses implementation challenges, including data privacy, teacher readiness, infrastructure, and the need for human-centered AI design. Keywords: artificial intelligence, student engagement, AI-based learning environment, learning analytics, adaptive feedback, personalized learning
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Persistent personal AI agents may change the relationship between an individual's attention and productive capacity. This paper defines Agentomaly as a proposed transition in which individuals can affordably sustain adaptive, concurrent delegated work that previously required more direct attention or organizational support. Delegation and automation are not new. The hypothesis concerns a change in their accessibility, flexibility, persistence, and coordination cost at the level of the individual principal. The paper distinguishes three questions: whether agents expand individual productive capacity; whether their interactions become a substantial operational layer of the economy; and whether the resulting systems preserve meaningful human authority. These outcomes need not coincide. A closed platform could deliver large productivity gains while concentrating control and making exit difficult. The proposed analytical unit is the principal-agent relationship. Its performance should be evaluated through quality-adjusted completed outcomes, principal attention, total human labor, elapsed time, resource cost, and externalities. More agent activity is not evidence of more economic value. The paper also develops the Principal Concentration Problem: many agent identities may represent one controlling organization rather than independent market participants. A governance framework addresses bounded mandates, audit, continuity, portability, and human re-entry. These are design commitments to assess separately from productivity, not assumed consequences of technical capability. A research agenda proposes comparisons with manual work, AI-assisted work, conventional automation, and human delegation. The 2030 horizon is a scenario boundary, not a forecast. The contribution is an integrated framework for testing when persistent delegation expands individual agency, how its benefits and costs are distributed, and whether its expansion remains subject to effective human control.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This chapter advances a decolonial framework for the epistemic stakes of AI-augmented thinking pedagogy in global higher education. Without deliberate intervention, the integration of generative AI into design thinking risks operationalising at a computational scale the colonial knowledge hierarchies long carried in less visible form by design thinking as a travelling pedagogy of Anglo-American provenance. The argument synthesises three theoretical resources. Fricker&s;s account of testimonial and hermeneutical injustice, extended through Dotson&s;s analysis of contributory injustice, supplies the framework&s;s analytic architecture. Santos&s;s diagnosis of abyssal thinking locates these harms within the longer history of epistemic colonialism, while Mignolo&s;s colonial matrix of power and political horizon of pluriversality orient the analysis toward pedagogical reconstruction rather than incremental adjustment. From this synthesis the chapter develops a three-dimensional framework identifying testimonial, hermeneutical, and contributory justice as conditions for responsible AI integration. A worked example from an undergraduate Gulf university course, in which students engage Syrian refugee educational experiences through refugee-authored sources rather than direct fieldwork, illustrates the framework alongside its ethical and institutional conditions. The chapter recasts AI ethics as a question of pedagogical formation for which educators and institutions, not technical systems, bear principal responsibility.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: As artificial intelligence reshapes the epistemic foundations of teaching, educators face unprecedented decisions about which knowledge practices to preserve, delegate or transform. This study introduces ‘epistemic negotiation’ as a conceptual lens to examine how educators actively deliberate about AI’s boundaries in knowledge work rather than passively accepting or rejecting technology. Moving beyond adoption-focused research, the study presents a typological analysis of AI-mediated Knowledge Management (KM) amongst 454 Indian educators. Using exploratory factor analysis and k-means clustering, four distinct profiles were identified: Disengaged, Instrumental Users, Process-Focused and High-fidelity Users, differentiated by epistemic orientations rather than technical competence. The findings reposition AI integration as primarily a knowledge management challenge. Theoretically, the study advances KM frameworks for analysing educational technology. Practically, the findings demonstrate that professional development must cultivate epistemic reflexivity and KM competencies over technical skills. For policy, the typology challenges uniform mandates, advocating differentiated support structures that honour diverse knowledge practices whilst establishing ethical parameters.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Erdőfigyelő (Hungarian for “forest watcher”; forest.equora.institute) is a public web system that links citizen reports on forests and water, open satellite change alerts, and forest-compartment records from the Hungarian National Forest Stand Database (NÉBIH) on a single map. This white paper describes the architecture, the data sources and the processing methods — a forest mask, cell-based patch delineation, the per-patch daily alerted area, pixel-level intersection with Natura 2000 sites and a single-date 2021 tree-cover flag from ESA WorldCover — as well as report moderation and privacy-by-design measures. First results as of 30 September 2026: between 1 January and 21 September 2026, 3,734 DIST-ALERT patches of at least 3 ha were recorded within the forest mask (total patch area 30,994.5 ha). Of the tree cover loss in Hungary between 2001 and 2017 (approx. 182 kha), 81.7% falls on cells classified as tree cover in ESA WorldCover 2021. In the Börzsöny sample area, 87.4% of the 582.8 ha alerted in the third quarter of 2026 lies within Natura 2000 sites. Pixel-level intermediate results are published, so that the area figures can be recomputed independently. The paper documents the limitations, the corrections made after human testing and three rounds of AI-assisted audits (ChatGPT-6 Astra) under the EQUORA Trilith Method™, with a dated correction log, and a research agenda led by a pre-specified, stratified national validation with drone-based field verification (Olofsson et al. 2014; Stehman 2014). Version 1.1 adds the third audit round, annual areas by pixel year for the 2024–2025 patches, both named measures for the sample boundary, explicit accuracy estimators and a Research Card. Files: English version (erdofigyelo-white-paper-v1.1-en.pdf) and Hungarian version (erdofigyelo-white-paper-v1.1-hu.pdf).Open data (CC BY 4.0): forest.equora.institute/nyilt-adat Magyar összefoglaló. Az Erdőfigyelő nyilvános webes rendszer, amely egy térképen kapcsolja össze a lakossági erdő- és vízügyi bejelentéseket, a nyilvános műholdas változásjelzéseket és a NÉBIH erdőrészlet-adatait. A dokumentum a rendszer felépítését, módszertanát, első eredményeit, korlátait és kutatási tervét írja le; a magyar változat a második fájl.

documents.abstract: This article highlights the importance of the principles of medical ethics and deontology in the professional activities of healthcare workers. Particular attention is paid to humanism, respect, trust, professional responsibility, medical confidentiality, respect for patients’ rights, and informed consent in the relationship between healthcare workers and patients. The article also analyzes new deontological issues arising in modern medicine, including the use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence, protection of patient data, and compliance with professional ethical standards when using social media.The communicative competence of healthcare workers, the culture of teamwork, and the prevention of occupational stress are also considered important factors in ensuring the quality of medical care. Keywords: medical ethics, deontology, healthcare worker, patient, professional responsibility, medical confidentiality, informed consent, communication, patients’ rights

documents.abstract: Fairness is one of the fundamental ethical principles governing the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education. AI systems increasingly influence learning recommendations, assessment, student support, admissions, academic advising, and institutional decision-making. Because these systems can affect educational opportunities, fairness must be considered throughout their design, development, deployment, and evaluation. An AI system is not automatically fair simply because it uses mathematical or computational methods. If the data, assumptions, objectives, or decision processes contain bias, the resulting system may reproduce or amplify existing inequalities. A simplified framework is: Educational Data → AI Model → Prediction/Recommendation → Educational Decision → Student Outcome Fairness requires examining every stage of this process. Fairness in AI-based education refers to the principle that learners should be treated equitably and should not experience unjustified disadvantage because of characteristics unrelated to legitimate educational objectives.Fairness involves: Equal opportunity Non-discrimination Appropriate treatment Inclusive access Consistent evaluation Protection from unjustified bias Fairness does not always mean treating every learner identically. Different learners may require different forms of support to achieve equitable educational opportunities. The major objectives include: Reducing discriminatory outcomes Providing equitable educational opportunities Identifying and reducing algorithmic bias Supporting inclusive learning Ensuring equitable access to AI systems Protecting vulnerable learners Promoting trustworthy educational technologies Fairness should be considered throughout: Data Collection → Model Development → Testing → Deployment → Monitoring A system that is fair during development may produce unfair outcomes after deployment if the educational environment changes. AI systems learn from data. If historical educational data contain unequal patterns, an AI system may reproduce them. For example: Historical Bias → Training Data → AI Model → Potentially Biased Prediction

documents.abstract: Ergonomics is a scientific discipline that aims to adapt working conditions to individuals' capabilities and limitations in order to improve safety, well-being, and job performance. In the educational context, its application is essential for protecting teachers' occupational health, as they are exposed to various ergonomic risk factors throughout their workday. The objective of this study was to evaluate the ergonomic conditions of teachers' workstations in an educational institution using the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) method. A quantitative, descriptive, and cross-sectional approach was employed, analyzing the postures adopted during the main teaching activities. The findings revealed that prolonged writing on the blackboard obtained a RULA score of 7, indicating a very high-risk level that requires immediate intervention. Likewise, prolonged use of technological devices reached a score of 6, while reviewing academic tasks and prolonged standing each obtained scores of 5, classifying these activities as high risk. It is concluded that preventive and corrective ergonomic measures should be implemented to reduce the identified risks and prevent the development of musculoskeletal disorders among teaching staff.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Background Office workers accumulate most of their waking h in sedentary behavior, yet scalable personalized occupational-health advice remains limited, and the quality of large language model (LLM)-based tools in this domain has not been rigorously examined. Objective This study evaluated whether a domain-specialized chatbot system for providing health advice on sedentary behavior, integrating retrieval augmentation, a curated corpus, and safety guardrails, performs better than a general-purpose LLM and static educational materials. Methods A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was used. In the blinded expert evaluation, nine raters independently rated 60 responses across five quality dimensions. In the user survey, 654 eligible Chinese office workers interacted with the specialized chatbot and completed six perception scales (two adapted from established technology-acceptance frameworks and four developed for this study) plus open-ended feedback. Results Inter-rater reliability was good for the composite score; in a case-level safety screen, no response from the specialized chatbot or the standard materials was flagged as potentially unsafe, whereas two Doubao responses were flagged by two or more raters. The specialized chatbot achieved the highest composite rating, followed by Doubao and standard materials. In a linear mixed-effects model and crossed random intercepts for rater and question, all Holm-adjusted pairwise contrasts were significant. Advantages of the specialized chatbot over Doubao were most pronounced on safety in symptom-management and special-population items. Among users, perceived ease of use was highest, whereas perceived safety and intention to use were rated comparatively lower. Frequent prior AI-chatbot use was associated with higher ratings on all six scales; after covariate adjustment the association persisted for five of the six scales but was attenuated and no longer significant for perceived safety. Conclusion The specialized chatbot system received expert-rated accuracy and safety scores that did not differ significantly from standard educational materials, but exceeded standard materials on usefulness, comprehensibility, and completeness, and outperformed the general-purpose LLM on accuracy, safety, completeness, and the overall composite score. These findings concern response quality and immediate user perceptions, not behavioral or clinical outcomes. Nonetheless, users remained cautious about safety and intention to use after this brief exposure.

Care-plan formulation is among the most cognitively demanding competencies that pre-registration nursing students must master, and errors made at this formative stage may persist into qualified practice. Two contemporary developments converge on this competency: the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) capable of suggesting nursing diagnoses and interventions, and the normalization of the telemedicine practicum as a clinical learning environment. No prior synthesis has examined their intersection. The aim of this study is to identify, appraise, and synthesize the evidence on the effect of AI-driven CDSS on the accuracy of nursing students’ care-plan formulation within telemedicine practicum settings. The review is designed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and conducted with reference to the Cochrane Handbook and the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis. Eight databases and grey-literature sources searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies published between 2015 and 2026. Screening, extraction, and appraisal were performed in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed with design-appropriate instruments (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, JBI checklists, MMAT), and certainty was rated using GRADE. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, and a structured narrative synthesis following SWiM guidance was undertaken. The evidence converges on a conditional benefit. Structured, taxonomy-aligned decision support raised students’ diagnostic and care-plan accuracy relative to unsupported practice, with the inference model, the supervision arrangement, and learner characteristics acting as decisive moderators. Generative large language models produced substantial gains in rated plan quality but exhibited a characteristic failure mode of fluent yet taxonomy-discordant output, creating conditions in which automation bias is most hazardous. The telemedicine setting amplified both the potential benefit and the risk of uncritical reliance. The study concludes that an AI-driven CDSS functions as a conditional cognitive scaffold rather than an unconditional accelerator of accuracy. Its educational value in the telemedicine practicum is realized only where outputs are aligned with recognized nursing taxonomies, system reasoning is transparent, and use is embedded within supervised, deliberate practice that preserves the student as the accountable clinical reasoner. Recommendations are made for nursing education, policy, and future primary research.

Objectives: This study aimed to compare the performance of DeepSeek-V3, ChatGPT 4.0, ChatGPT 4.5, Gemini Advanced 2.0, and Grok in answering single-correct answer multiple-choice (SCQ), multiple-correct answer multiple-choice (MCQ), binary (true/false) (BQ), and open-ended questions (OEQ) based on the European Society of Endodontology (ESE) position statements.Materials and Methods: A total of 70 questions (24 SCQ/MCQ, 29 BQ, and 17 OEQ) were posed to five LLMs. Responses were scored on a 0–10 scale for comprehensiveness, scientific accuracy, clarity, and relevance. SCQ, MCQ, and BQ formats were additionally evaluated for correctness (1 = correct, 0 = incorrect). Data were analyzed using Pearson’s chi-square test and the Kruskal-Wallis H test (p < 0.05).Results: In the SCQ/MCQ format, Gemini Advanced 2.0 scored significantly higher than Grok. In the BQ format, ChatGPT 4.5 and Gemini Advanced 2.0 achieved significantly higher scores than ChatGPT 4.0 and Grok. In the OEQ format, ChatGPT 4.5 obtained significantly higher scores than Grok (p < 0.05). Accuracy rates were 67.9% for ChatGPT 4.5, 66.0% for Gemini Advanced 2.0, 58.5% for DeepSeek-V3, 52.8% for ChatGPT 4.0, and 49.1% for Grok (p > 0.05). In all models, scientific accuracy scores were significantly lower than relevance scores (p < 0.05).Conclusions: ChatGPT 4.5 and Gemini Advanced 2.0 demonstrated stronger performance than the other models, whereas Grok showed lower response-content performance. However, since LLMs may appear convincing even when generating incorrect clinical information, they should be used only as supplementary tools in endodontic education and preliminary information retrieval. Clinically relevant outputs should be verified by an endodontist or an appropriately qualified clinician.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The well-being of educators is a cornerstone of high-quality education. However, teachers in the expanding global private school sector face significant workplace stressors. Increasing competition and pressure to perform can negatively impact both student achievement and school climate by increasing workloads and burnout. This study examines the relationship between psychosocial risks and job satisfaction among private school teachers in Türkiye, a country with a globally competitive education environment. This research focused on private school teachers working in Erzurum province. Data were collected using Google forms after obtaining ethics committee approval. Using a cross-sectional design, 203 teachers were surveyed using the Copenhagen Psychosocial Risk Questionnaire (COPSOQ-TR) and Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ). The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 25 software, employing descriptive statistics, normality (Shapiro-Wilk) and homogeneity of variance (Levene) tests, t-tests, the Mann-Whitney U test, ANOVA, the Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal-Wallis test, and Spearman’s correlation analysis. Statistical analysis revealed a strong and significant negative correlation between general psychosocial risk and job satisfaction (r = -.803, p < .001). In particular, it was found that organizational factors such as weak leadership, lack of fairness, and insufficient recognition had a greater negative impact on satisfaction than workload demands. The importance of a supportive and fair organizational environment has been emphasized. Additionally, a positive correlation was found between burnout and job satisfaction, suggesting the existence of a complex “commitment paradox” among highly dedicated teachers in the field. Demographic characteristics, such as gender, age, teaching experience, marital status, and whether teachers had received occupational health and safety (OHS) training, also significantly influenced the perception of specific risks, such as burnout and work-family conflict. These findings underscore the need for systematic interventions. Proactive risk management, leadership development focused on promoting fairness and support, and policies aimed at enhancing teachers’ resilience are vital. Protecting teachers’ well-being is not only a necessity from an occupational health perspective, but also a direct investment in maintaining the quality of education.

This study examines the role of the exchange rate as an interactive predictor in artificial intelligence (AI) models for financial distress prediction in Iraqi private banks. Earlier financial-distress studies have primarily emphasized bank-specific financial ratios or have treated macroeconomic variables as additive controls. The present study instead investigates whether exchange-rate conditions modify the relationship between bank-specific financial indicators and the probability of distress. The empirical analysis uses a panel of 170 bank-year observations for 10 Iraqi private banks listed on the Iraq Stock Exchange over the period 2008–2024. Logistic Regression is used as the conventional benchmark, while Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Artificial Neural Network models are used as machine-learning alternatives; Cox proportional hazards analysis is additionally used to examine interaction effects in a time-to-distress framework. The comparative results show that Random Forest achieved the highest reported classification performance, with an accuracy of 98.1%, sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 100%, F1-score of 92.3%, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.898. Interaction analysis indicates that the exchange rate significantly moderates the association between non-performing loans and financial distress and also modifies the effect of selected profitability indicators. Decision-tree rules further reveal exchange-rate thresholds that alter distress classification conditional on profitability and credit quality. Variable-importance analyses consistently place profitability, credit quality, and the exchange rate among the most influential predictors. These findings support an interaction-based interpretation of banking risk in which macroeconomic conditions change the informational value of bank-specific indicators rather than merely adding an independent source of risk. The study contributes to the financial-distress literature by integrating model comparison, interaction analysis, and interpretable

This study, focusing on sustainable energy production and particularly the hydrogen (H 2 ) economy, presents an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) framework for accurately predicting H 2 production from sucrose photocatalysis catalyzed by LaFeO 3 (GLFO) and the H 2 concentration in syngas derived from biomass conversion. The research was conducted along two main directions: (i) deep learning (DL) architectures comprising nine specially designed recurrent neural network-based models and (ii) six conventional machine learning (ML) algorithms. For both H 2 production systems, the best-performing models were identified and further interpreted using explainable AI (XAI) based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Among all investigated algorithms, a hybrid One-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network–Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory–Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (1D-CNN–BiLSTM–BiGRU) model demonstrated the highest predictive performance. Using 10-fold cross-validation, the proposed model achieved outstanding accuracy, with an R 2 value of 0.9987 ± 0.0011 for photocatalytic H 2 production prediction and 0.9980 ± 0.0006 for syngas H 2 concentration prediction. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework as a precise, reliable, and practical methodological approach for modeling and optimizing complex thermochemical energy systems.

The study identifies the organizational factors that contribute to the development of burnout syndrome among professionals in the health, education, and telecommunications sectors in the Baixada Fluminense region, part of the metropolitan area of the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. This is an exploratory study with a qualitative approach. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews with seven professionals, and the empirical material was analyzed following Bardin’s content analysis procedures. The results indicate that factors such as work overload, micromanagement, lack of autonomy, and a high-pressure environment are determinants of emotional exhaustion, reduced productivity, and high staff turnover. Participants identified work overload and the accumulation of duties, limited autonomy, pressure related to goals and deadlines, and insufficient organizational support as the main organizational factors. Several interviewees reported difficulties disconnecting from work, interference with their personal lives, fatigue, stress, and a perceived deterioration in emotional well-being. Some also reported having considered leaving their jobs. Most participants did not identify specific organizational actions aimed at preventing burnout, although one divergent experience involving institutional emotional health initiatives was observed. It is concluded that the absence of effective organizational strategies for burnout prevention perpetuates the vulnerability of these workers, reinforcing the urgent need for more localized and effective occupational health policies.

Abstract Rotating machines are widely employed in modern industry. The growing demand for efficiency and operational durability drives the development of intelligent rotors equipped with Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods that promote the extension of equipment lifespan through proactive maintenance actions and reducing costs associated with unscheduled downtime. Some common failures in rotating machines, such as unbalance, misalignment, and cracks, have similar symptoms, making it difficult to diagnose accurately. The absence of labeled historical data and explainable models that are understandable to end users also makes using AI difficult in the industry environment. This work presents a fault diagnosis technique based on vibration analysis and explainable AI models in this context. The proposed methodology achieved high diagnostic performance, with precision, recall, and F1-score exceeding 98.9% in numerical tests and demonstrating robust accuracy in experimental scenarios using a reduced set of 12 features. The methodology is demonstrated with interpretable applications that facilitate real-time fault diagnosis and proactive maintenance in rotating machinery, showcasing its potential for industrial implementation. Vibration responses are obtained through a representative finite element (FE) model of a horizontal rotor and its corresponding test rig. Techniques for feature extraction and selection are also employed. Ensemble clustering is performed for novelty detection, while traditional supervised approaches are used for classification purposes. The explainable AI tool is used to interpret the results, revealing that features such as the second harmonic of the rotational speed (A2X-S1) and skewness (R08-S1), both extracted from plane S1 in axial direction, play a critical role in distinguishing between similar fault patterns. The combination of robust performance and the possibility of interpretation from the output models demonstrates the potential of the proposed approach for fault recognition in rotating systems.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Accurate measurement of behaviors is critical for research in human-computer interaction, ubiquitous computing, and personal health informatics, because it underpins many health tracking and intervention systems. Most data collection studies, however, still rely on participants' self-reports and manual annotations, which often under- or over-estimate activity duration and type, and require substantial effort from researchers to clean and validate. An automated system that can combine passive sensing data with participants' self-reports might detect inconsistencies and suggest corrections. We introduce GLOSS4HAR, a multi-agent LLM-based system designed to mimic human sensemaking and assist researchers in cleaning and refining activity annotations. We demonstrate the potential of GLOSS4HAR in two key tasks: (1) correcting and reconciling participant self-annotations, and (2) triangulating passive sensing data with different forms of lightweight self-reports to generate accurate activity timelines. Our evaluation shows that GLOSS4HAR improves annotation quality by up to 9.9% in F1 score and can reconstruct activity timelines that align with human annotations at 75-92% F1. Based on our findings, we discuss the implications of our work for the next generation of activity annotation systems that might use human-AI collaboration.
topics: Personal Information Management and User Behavior

documents.abstract: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs)-synthesized data to enable representation learning for cold-start entities has emerged as a promising solution for addressing cold-start recommendations. However, existing studies often over-rely on LLM-generated data while neglecting the detrimental noise it may introduce. This work investigates data filtering mechanisms to remove detrimental synthetic samples. One promising approach is to use influence functions to measure the influence of each data. Nevertheless, a technical challenge arises because accurate influence estimation requires an unbiased reference model, which cannot be satisfied due to the existence of unknown noise. To address this, we conduct a theoretical analysis, revealing that when the goal is to identify a small subset of highly harmful data, even a biased model can still reliably capture the most detrimental points. Building on this insight, we propose a Progressive Influence Function-based method (PIF) for data filtering. PIF iteratively refines influence estimates: it repeatedly trains a new reference model after removing the previous step's most harmful data and reassesses influence. As detrimental data is progressively removed, the reference model becomes less biased. Finally, PIF ensembles influence estimates across iterations for robust filtering. Extensive experiments validate the efficacy of our approach.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technological innovations of the twenty-first century, fundamentally changing the way individuals learn, work, communicate, and solve complex problems. Although AI has become a prominent component of modern society only in recent decades, its conceptual foundations extend back several centuries through philosophical discussions concerning human intelligence, logical reasoning, and mechanical computation. The evolution of Artificial Intelligence represents a multidisciplinary journey involving computer science, mathematics, cognitive psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, philosophy, engineering, statistics, and data science. Continuous advancements in computational power, algorithmic development, data availability, and digital infrastructure have enabled AI to evolve from theoretical concepts into intelligent systems capable of performing tasks that traditionally required human intelligence. The earliest ideas related to artificial intelligence originated long before the invention of computers. Ancient civilizations imagined intelligent machines capable of mimicking human behaviour through myths, literature, and mechanical inventions. During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, philosophers and mathematicians such as René Descartes, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, and George Boole contributed foundational concepts related to logic, reasoning, symbolic representation, and mathematical computation. Their work laid the intellectual groundwork for the development of computational systems capable of representing knowledge and making logical decisions.The modern evolution of Artificial Intelligence began during the twentieth century with the rapid advancement of computing technologies. In the 1930s and 1940s, significant progress in mathematical logic and computer science established the theoretical basis for intelligent machines. Alan Turing introduced the concept of a universal computing machine and later proposed the famous Turing Test, which examined whether a machine could demonstrate behaviour indistinguishable from that of a human being. Turing's pioneering contributions remain fundamental to contemporary AI research because they established that machines could potentially perform intelligent reasoning through computational processes. A major milestone occurred in 1956 during the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, organized by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon, and Nathaniel Rochester. This conference formally introduced the term "Artificial Intelligence" and established AI as an independent scientific discipline. Researchers believed that human intelligence could be represented computationally and that machines could eventually perform reasoning, learning, language understanding, and problem-solving. The Dartmouth Conference inspired widespread academic interest and initiated decades of intensive research into intelligent computing systems.The period between the late 1950s and early 1970s is often referred to as the early development phase of Artificial Intelligence. During this era, researchers developed symbolic AI methods that emphasized logical reasoning, rule-based systems, theorem proving, and problem-solving algorithms. Early AI programmes successfully solved mathematical problems, played strategic games such as chess, and demonstrated limited natural language capabilities. Optimism surrounding AI research increased substantially as scientists believed that general human-level intelligence could be achieved within a relatively short period. However, limitations in computing power, data availability, memory capacity, and algorithmic efficiency restricted further progress. During the 1970s and 1980s, Artificial Intelligence experienced periods commonly known as the "AI Winters," characterized by reduced research funding, slower technological progress, and diminished public expectations. Many ambitious predictions regarding human-level machine intelligence proved unrealistic because available computing resources and algorithms were insufficient to support increasingly complex AI applications. Deep learning has become one of the most influential developments in contemporary Artificial Intelligence. Inspired by the structure of the human brain, deep neural networks consist of multiple computational layers capable of learning complex representations from large datasets. These architectures have dramatically improved performance in image recognition, speech processing, language translation, autonomous driving, medical imaging, recommendation systems, fraud detection, and scientific research. documents.abstract: Background The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into workplace practices has reshaped how employees process information and perform cognitive tasks. While these systems are often associated with superior efficiency, their excessive use may entail significant cognitive costs. Objective Grounded in automation complacency perspective and the growing literature on technology addiction, this study investigates how dependence on artificial intelligence is associated with cognitive engagement in the workplace, with particular attention to the mediating role of cognitive fatigue. Methods Adopting quantitative research design, data were collected from 246 academic and administrative staff who actively use AI tools in their daily work routines. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the theoretical model proposed. Results The findings indicate that dependence on AI was positively associated with cognitive fatigue (β = 0.569; t = 13.468; p = 0.000) and negatively with cognitive engagement (β = −0.174; t = 2.503; p = 0.012). In addition, the relationship between cognitive fatigue and cognitive engagement was found to be negative and statistically significant (β = −0.207; t = 2.773; p = 0.006). Mediation analysis further revealed that cognitive fatigue partially mediates the relationship between dependence on AI and cognitive engagement (indirect effect β = −0.118, t = 2.724, p < .01; VAF = 40.5%). Conclusion These results suggest that higher levels of dependence on AI correspond to higher employee cognitive fatigue, which in turn relates to lower cognitive engagement at work. By empirically demonstrating the cognitive costs of AI reliance, this study contributes to the emerging literature on workplace AI and technology addiction.

Abstract This study examines the transition from automation to generative AI in professional communication, focusing on human–AI co-creativity. While earlier research framed AI mainly as an efficiency tool, the rapid emergence of generative AI has reconfigured communication practices toward collaborative and co-creative models. This structured literature synthesis, informed by PRISMA reporting principles, synthesizes empirical research published between 2012 and 2026 across journalism, public relations, strategic communication, and digital media, investigating how generative AI is integrated into creative workflows and how communicative agency is distributed between human professionals and AI systems. The results identify four dimensions shaping human–AI co-creativity: (1) AI affordances enabling ideation while introducing constraints such as algorithmic opacity; (2) human professional agency, through which practitioners retain interpretive authority via prompt design; (3) organizational context, structuring AI adoption; and (4) ethical and cultural norms concerning transparency and accountability. The review advances conceptual clarity on human–AI co-creativity as an emergent sociotechnical process, arguing that generative AI is not simply augmenting communication work but fundamentally reshaping how creativity, authorship, and responsibility are enacted. documents.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence–driven chatbots into digital commerce has transformed firm–consumer interactions, shifting the focus from efficiency-oriented automation toward more human-centered engagement. In this context, anthropomorphic chatbot design has emerged as a key mechanism through which firms seek to introduce human touch into AI-mediated interactions and influence consumer purchase intention. Despite growing scholarly attention, existing research on chatbot anthropomorphism remains fragmented across disciplines, limiting a comprehensive understanding of its intellectual structure, theoretical foundations, and thematic evolution. To address this gap, the present study conducts a PRISMA 2020–guided bibliometric and systematic review of research published between 2016 and 2025. Drawing on a bibliometric dataset of 200 publications and a systematically screened subset of 80 high-quality studies, the analysis employs VOSviewer to examine publication trends, keyword co-occurrence patterns, and co-authorship networks. The findings reveal a clear progression in the literature from automation-focused chatbot applications toward human-centered AI interactions emphasizing anthropomorphism, social presence, and relational mechanisms. The results identify anthropomorphic design, human touch, trust, and consumer engagement as central themes shaping purchase intention in chatbot-mediated environments. By integrating anthropomorphism theory, social presence theory, and the Computers as Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, the study proposes a theory-driven framework explaining how human-like chatbot cues activate perceptions of human touch, which subsequently foster trust and influence consumer buying behavior. Beyond consolidating fragmented literature, this study advances theoretical understanding of human-centered AI and offers actionable insights for managers seeking to design effective chatbot interactions in digital commerce. The findings also highlight promising avenues for future research, including contextual, cross cultural, and ethical considerations in anthropomorphic AI design.

The transformation of knowledge from the classical Islamic tradition to the modern era and Artificial Intelligence (AI) demonstrates not only the growth of knowledge but also shifts in its sources, methods, validity, and authority. However, studies on Bayt al-Hikmah, the development of modern science, Islamic epistemology, and AI in Islamic education tend to be discussed in separate domains. Consequently, the connection between these epistemological transformations and scientific integration in Islamic education has not been systematically examined. This study aims to analyze the epistemological transformation of knowledge from classical scholarly traditions through Bayt al-Hikmah, the development of modern science, to the AI era, and to examine its relevance to scientific integration in Islamic education. This study employs a qualitative approach with a library research method. Literature was analyzed descriptively and analytically across four dimensions: sources, methods, validity, and authority of knowledge. The findings indicate that Bayt al-Hikmah represents an open scientific paradigm toward various traditions through translation, dialogue, critique, and knowledge development. Modern science subsequently reinforced scientific methods, observation, experimentation, and empirical proof, though the rise of specialization also risks driving scientific fragmentation. The contribution of this study lies in its continuous reading of these transformations through four epistemological dimensions and their connection to the integrative-interconnective paradigm in Islamic education. In this context, scientific integration needs to connect revelation, reason, empirical experience, technology, and ethical and spiritual values. AI should be positioned as an instrument for knowledge development that remains subject to human verification, interpretation, and ethical judgment.

This work presents a theoretical architecture for continually adapting AI systems organized around three distinct timescales: (1) fast transformer key-value context for immediate interaction, (2) medium-term persistent recurrent memory with decaying importance and consolidation, and (3) slow, controlled parameter adaptation. The proposed pathway is context → persistent memory → importance estimation → consolidation → plasticity gating → bounded parameter update → changed future computation. The manuscript formalizes recurrent state dynamics, transformer attention, gated persistent memory, exponential importance decay, importance-biased retrieval, prediction loss, gated online updates, consolidation thresholds, and learned update rules. It also explains why adapting recurrent transition weights such as U changes state-transition dynamics, whereas updating memory changes stored state without necessarily changing the underlying transition rule. The package distinguishes inference-time state adaptation, memory adaptation, online parameter learning, meta-learning, recursive self-learning, and recursive self-improvement. It proposes controlled experiments comparing transformer, KV-context, persistent-memory, importance, consolidation, gated-update, and learned-update variants, with metrics for retention, transfer, forgetting, poisoning robustness, parameter drift, retrieval quality, and compute cost. This is a conceptual research architecture and falsifiable research hypothesis. It reports no experimental measurements and does not claim AGI, consciousness, human-level cognition, biological equivalence, or open-ended recursive self-improvement. The prefrontal-cortex comparison is functional only, referring to working-memory maintenance, goal persistence, error monitoring, and adaptive control. AI assistance disclosure: ChatGPT assisted with manuscript drafting, mathematical editing, structure, and package preparation. Final authorship and publication decisions remain with Chaman Prakash Kanth. Sarvam AI was also used.

documents.abstract: Literature is a mirror of society. It shows the economic conditions, social problems, and daily struggles of human life across different times. Work is one of the most important parts of human life. In the past, many people depended completely on land, rich masters, or family heads for their survival. Over time, the meaning of work has changed from total dependence to economic independence. English literature presents many stories of characters who fight against poverty and social rules to earn their own living and live with dignity. Work is not just a way to earn money; it also gives a person self-respect, identity, and personal freedom. This research paper examines how work, economy, and independence are presented in selected English literary texts: Charlotte Brontë’s Jane Eyre, Elizabeth Gaskell’s North and South, and Virginia Woolf’s A Room of One’s Own. These texts show how education, employment, and money help individuals to become free and confident. Finally, this paper connects these literary lessons with the modern world. Today, technology, artificial intelligence, online platforms, and work-from-home jobs are changing the future of work. The paper concludes that even in the modern digital age, human dignity and economic security are essential for true freedom.

Abstract India’s vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a digital governance architecture that can transform rapidly expanding volumes of public data into timely, evidence-based, inclusive, transparent, and sustainable policy outcomes. This paper develops an integrated conceptual framework for data-driven digital governance by examining the complementary roles of Data Analytics, Business Intelligence (BI), Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI). Drawing on conceptual analysis and secondary evidence, the study conceptualizes DPI as the foundational layer for interoperable and trusted digital services, while Data Analytics and BI enable the transformation of data into descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive intelligence. Responsible AI further strengthens forecasting, simulation, decision support, and adaptive governance while incorporating principles of transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, security, and human oversight. A key contribution of the study is the proposed six-level BI maturity model, progressing from Digitization and Reporting to Diagnostic BI, Predictive Analytics, Decision Intelligence, and Adaptive Governance. The model addresses the challenge of dashboard-oriented governance by emphasising the progression from data availability to actionable intelligence, informed decision-making, outcome measurement, and continuous policy feedback. The study also identifies critical barriers, including data fragmentation, interoperability constraints, privacy and cybersecurity risks, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, institutional capability gaps, and inadequate outcome measurement. To address these challenges, a phased 2027–2047 strategic roadmap is proposed, beginning with common data standards and institutional analytics capacity and progressing toward interoperable, AI-assisted, outcome-oriented, and continuously learning governance systems. The paper argues that India’s long-term digital governance advantage will depend not merely on achieving digitalization at population scale, but on developing the institutional and technological capacity to convert data into intelligence, intelligence into informed decisions, and decisions into measurable and inclusive public value.

documents.abstract: The evolution of digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the role of libraries in society. Libraries that were once physical repositories of printed material are now providing greater access to e-books, e-journals, digital repositories, online databases, and institutional resources. The next frontier in this evolution is the creation of intelligent knowledge hubs, enabled by new technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing, natural language processing, and multilingual systems. Intelligent libraries have the potential to be critical knowledge infrastructures for education, research, innovation, digital literacy, skill development, and lifelong learning in the context of Viksit Bharat @2047. Digital resources and remote information services can help bridge the knowledge divide between rural and urban communities, while multilingual digital content can enhance information access for a diverse range of users. At the same time, the development of intelligent knowledge hubs also presents a number of challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, financial constraints, skills gaps, data privacy, cybersecurity, copyright, and ethical issues around AI. Consequently, technological development needs to be supported by well-trained library professionals, robust security measures, ethical practices, and user-focused policies. By taking an inclusive and sustainable approach, intelligent libraries can play a significant role in advancing a knowledge-driven, digitally empowered, and inclusive Viksit Bharat @2047

documents.abstract: Abstract : Gatekeeping has remained one of the foundational theoretical approaches for explaining how information becomes news. From Kurt Lewin’s conceptualisation of gates and channels to David Manning White’s study of the newspaper wire editor, traditional gatekeeping theory located considerable power in human actors who selected, rejected and organised information before it reached audiences. The contemporary news environment, however, complicates this model. News selection is increasingly distributed across journalists, newsroom analytics, search engines, social media platforms, recommender systems and generative artificial intelligence. This paper re-examines gatekeeping theory through an interdisciplinary synthesis of journalism studies, platform studies, artificial intelligence research and communication theory. Drawing on a structured conceptual review of more than 29 major scholarly contributions, it argues that contemporary journalism is moving from identifiable gatekeepers towards interconnected gatekeeping systems. Within these systems, editorial judgement has not disappeared; rather, it interacts continuously with computational selection, platform infrastructures, audience behaviour and generative systems capable of producing, summarising and reorganising information. The paper proposes a five-layer model of contemporary gatekeeping comprising source, editorial, algorithmic, platform and generative gates. It further distinguishes between selection power, traditionally exercised by editors, and visibility power, increasingly exercised through technological infrastructures. The study concludes that gatekeeping theory remains valuable but requires conceptual expansion from the question of who controls the gate to the broader question of how interconnected human and computational systems determine what information becomes visible, credible and socially consequential.

Purpose This study aims to examine how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-enabled knowledge creation processes influence entrepreneurial knowledge co-creation and small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) digital transformation through entrepreneurial general innovativeness and entrepreneurial specific innovativeness. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the socialization, externalization, combination and internalization (SECI) knowledge creation framework, the study develops and tests a mediation model linking GenAI internalization (GAI), GenAI externalization (GAE), GenAI socialization (GAS) and GenAI combination (GAC) with SME outcomes. Data was collected from 391 SME respondents and analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling in analysis of moment structures. Findings The findings show that GAI, GAE and GAC significantly enhance both entrepreneurial general innovativeness and entrepreneurial specific innovativeness. GAS significantly influences entrepreneurial specific innovativeness but does not significantly affect entrepreneurial general innovativeness. Both forms of entrepreneurial innovativeness positively influence entrepreneurial knowledge co-creation and SME digital transformation. Mediation results further show that entrepreneurial general innovativeness mediates the effects of GAI, GAE and GAC, while entrepreneurial specific innovativeness provides a more consistent mediating pathway across GenAI-enabled knowledge processes. Practical implications SME managers should use GenAI not merely for automation or content generation, but for learning, knowledge articulation, knowledge integration, innovation adoption and digital transformation. Originality/value The study advances GenAI entrepreneurship research by showing how GenAI-enabled SECI processes create SME value through entrepreneurial innovativeness.

This working paper develops the worldwide normative claim of Jean-Pol Martin’s New Human Rights (NMR) and semantic field. It examines how an organismic understanding of human life, basic needs and collective problem-solving can inform standards for education, institutions, community development and human-AI cooperation. The argument makes the normative bridge explicit: when the preservation and flourishing of human life, equal consideration of persons and the protection of shared life-supporting conditions are accepted as aims, societal decisions should be assessed by their effects on those conditions. The six NMR domains are thinking, health, security, social inclusion, self-realization and participation, and meaning. The New Human Rights articulate rights and aims; the semantic field provides a connected vocabulary for understanding situations, evaluating alternatives and organizing cooperative action. What this article adds:Normative orientation is already present in the existing framework. This paper’s specific contribution is its focused justification of worldwide normative use. It distinguishes anthropological description, normative commitments and institutional implications, and illustrates their connection through the participatory redesign of a public square. Function within the Zenodo corpus:The article connects the reconstruction of Martin’s theory architecture with public justification and practical decision criteria. It links existing strands on Learning by Teaching, New Human Rights, semantic coherence, prioritization, governance and human-AI cooperation. It thus serves as a bridge from conceptual synthesis to accountable societal application. Worldwide orientation is understood as shared evaluative concerns combined with context-sensitive implementation. The paper proposes a framework for public discussion and application; it does not claim existing international endorsement or legal recognition of the NMR. This is a conceptual working paper without a new empirical dataset. Jean-Pol Martin supplied the conceptual framework and direction. documents.abstract: Current ride-sharing platforms predominantly rely on subjective post-ride ratings to evaluate driver credibility, making reputation systems vulnerable to user bias, delayed feedback, collusion, and manipulation. Although recent studies have explored blockchain-based ride-sharing, AI-driven driver monitoring, and IoT-enabled transportation independently, they do not provide an integrated trust framework that continuously derives credibility from objectively verifiable driving behaviour while maintaining scalability and low operational cost.This paper presents Ridezy, a decentralized trust architecture that replaces conventional rating-based reputation with real-time sensor-driven credibility. The proposed framework combines edge Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (AIIoT) technologies to continuously monitor behavioural indicators such as lane discipline, speed compliance, braking behaviour, and traffic sign adherence. Instead of storing high-frequency telemetry on the blockchain, Ridezy employs a hybrid architecture in which behavioural summaries are processed off-chain and only cryptographic hashes, credibility updates, and payment records are anchored on Polygon smart contracts, enabling tamper-evident trust with minimal blockchain overhead. To evaluate the proposed architecture, Ridezy is compared against three representative trust models: a traditional rating-based system, an AI-only architecture, and a blockchain-only architecture. The evaluation considers behavioural detection performance, end-to-end latency, cost efficiency, throughput, reputation stability, tamper resistance, and component-wise ablation studies. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid architecture achieves higher behavioural fidelity and stronger trust guarantees than conventional reputation mechanisms while maintaining low per-ride blockchain cost and scalable operation through batched on-chain commitments.The primary contribution of this work is a sensor-driven credibility framework that transforms real-time behavioural evidence into a cryptographically verifiable trust primitive for ride-sharing ecosystems. By combining edge AI, IoT telemetry, and blockchain-based trust anchoring within a scalable hybrid architecture, Ridezy provides a practical foundation for trustworthy, transparent, and next-generation intelligent mobility systems.
